News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyokeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’ right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup winning substitutes – Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Odegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

News.title: Antonelli ends 60-year wait for home winner after starting 19th at Italian GP
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli showed why he appears to be Formula One’s champion-elect as he became the first Italian since Ludovico Scarfiotti 60 years ago to win his home race, despite starting 19th.

Antonelli, who elected to take a grid penalty at Monza for taking a new engine, spent the entire race hunting down Mercedes team-mate George Russell, finally passing the Briton on lap 50 of 53.

Antonelli benefited from an early red flag after Charles Leclerc smashed into the barriers at Parabolica on what was an awful day for Ferrari.

Antonelli also took advantage of a mid-race virtual safety car to switch tyres when Russell stayed out in the lead.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’s last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

News.title: ‘It’s just a useless gimmick’: Telegraph readers react to Dyson’s latest gadget
News.content:
Would you spend over £400 on a toothbrush? Telegraph readers aren’t convinced.

The new Dyson CameraJet has just launched, retailing for £419.99, which brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera.

After Rebecca Astill gave her verdict on the gadget, we asked Telegraph readers for their views and whether Dyson can convince them to trade in their old faithfuls.

They share the toothbrushes they swear by, from manual to electric models, and whether they see any reason to upgrade. Here’s what they had to say.

Why readers are unconvinced

The majority of readers seem unconvinced by the CameraJet, with John arguing that a toothbrush and a smartphone “sounds like two accidents waiting to happen. Squirted in the eye with mouthwash as you drop the phone down the toilet”.

“It’s just a useless gimmick,” argues reader Donald Mckie, a retired NHS dentist. “The average patient wouldn’t have a clue what they would be looking at in their mouth on a phone screen,” he adds.

“Dyson as a brand is an aspiration for many but I don’t know how this appliance would improve anyone’s oral health.”

In his view, “the tank for the mouthwash at 12.5ml is far too small, the industry average will be somewhere near 250-300ml” to last long enough and successfully dislodge sticky plaque.

He also questions the picture quality of the camera with water spray, saliva, lips, facial hair and toothpaste in the way. “People nowadays will expect pin sharp detail, which I doubt this will deliver.”

Sports.title: Three points from Man Utd’s draw at Everton with Michael Carrick putting himself in the firing line again
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have given their fans more food for thought with an eventful 2-2 draw at Everton.

The lead they took via Benjamin Sesko‘s 88th-minute header was wiped out deep into stoppage time by Ainsley Maitland-Niles‘ long-range stunner.



And that has left the Red Devils with just four points from their first three Premier League matches this term – all of which they went into as overwhelming favourites.

SunSport’s Samuel Luckhurst offers up his three talking points from Hill Dickinson Stadium…



TELL IT LIKE IT IS

Michael Carrick says United have not had a bad start, but he’s wrong.

When a United manager comes out with stuff like that, it is just going to wind up supporters.



Going forward, he needs to look after himself a little bit more and be a bit more critical of the team.

It’s just not going to chime with fans. He sounds a bit too compliant, like Ole Gunnar Solskjaer did during his tenure, and that didn’t really get him anywhere.



WATCH YOUR BACK

Defensively, United are in a state of disarray after conceding six goals in their first three games.

There is no defensive midfielder in that team at the moment because it took so long to sign Carlos Baleba, so there is no shield for the back-four.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But you look at the full-backs – Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot first started together eight years ago – so there is possibly some backwards thinking there.

Harry Maguire looked a little bit leggy. He has never been the quickest, but at 33 he is only going to get slower.

Lisandro Martinez is not particularly quick either.



United look so open and gettable. Everton had twice as many attempts on target, so if they were a bit more clinical, maybe they’d have had an even better day.

LAM TO THE SLAUGHTER

Senne Lammens probably had his worst game for United.

He dropped a pretty straightforward cross in the first half, punched away a catchable effort, and was culpable for Tyrique George‘s goal.



His handling was far too feeble at his near post. For his sake, he has to hope that is just an aberration.

But going forward, Lammens, the state of the United defence, it is lacking.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yes, they are probably going to address it next year.

But even when Carrick was asked about that, he said it was not guaranteed, which is also just going to wind up supporters.

Sports.title: Three points from Arsenal’s win over Chelsea as Arteta will be left feeling smug over questionable transfer policy
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA could hardly have asked for a better answer to the questions surrounding Arsenal’s summer transfer business.

The Premier League champions came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates and make it three wins from three to start their title defence.



Morgan Rogers, one of Arsenal’s big summer targets before his £117million move to Chelsea, threatened to make them regret missing out when he fired the visitors ahead after just 77 seconds.

But Kai Havertz levelled midway through the first half before skipper Martin Odegaard completed the turnaround after the break.



And with several of Arteta’s big calls paying off, SunSport looks at three talking points from another statement win.

Havertz outclassed his former club in style

Arsenal’s decision to leave themselves looking light in attack after the transfer window raised plenty of eyebrows.



Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard were all moved on, Ethan Nwaneri left on loan and Christos Tzolis was their only new wide attacking arrival.

But Havertz provided the perfect reminder of why Arteta was happy to stick with what he had.

The former Chelsea man dragged Arsenal level with his first-half strike before playing his part in the winner by allowing Tzolis’ delivery to run through for Odegaard.

Havertz may not always be the flashiest No9 in the Premier League but his movement, work-rate and intelligence remain hugely important to this Arsenal side.

Arsenal ratings vs Chelsea: Havertz reminds Blues of what they let go but Lewis-Skelly in second gear KAI HAVERTZ inspired an Arsenal fight-back as they beat London rivals Chelsea to continue their perfect start. The Gunners were chasing the game after their former transfer target, Morgan Rogers, volleyed the visitors ahead after just 77 seconds. But Arsenal kept their cool and equalised when Havertz fired inside the near post midway through the first half. Havertz then set up Arsenal’s second – even though he won’t get credited with the assist – as his excellent dummy created the space for Martin Odegaard to turn in from close range. Chelsea gave Havertz his break in Premier League football when they shelled out big money to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen in 2020. But he has enjoyed tormenting them – scoring four goals in seven head-to-heads – since he moved across the capital three years later. Here is the verdict of SunSport’s Simon Collings on how each Arsenal player performed…

And after Rogers had given Chelsea the lead, Arteta will have enjoyed seeing a player already in his building provide the response.

Konsa looks at home

Ezri Konsa was handed his first Arsenal start after arriving from Aston Villa in a deal worth around £51million last month.

The England defender came in for the injured Cristhian Mosquera and, despite Arsenal being rocked inside two minutes, soon settled alongside Gabriel.

Arteta has been criticised before for repeatedly spending big on defenders, but Konsa’s arrival already looks capable of giving him another reliable option across the back line.

With William Saliba sidelined long-term, Arsenal moved quickly for an experienced Premier League defender rather than gambling on their existing depth.



Against one of the league’s most dangerous attacks, that decision looked an increasingly sensible one.

Tzolis shows why Arsenal signed him

Tzolis arrived from Club Brugge for around £34m after producing 17 goals and 23 assists in their title-winning campaign last season.

And the Greece international showed another glimpse of why Arsenal were prepared to make him their main attacking addition.

His dangerous second-half ball eventually found Odegaard after Havertz’s clever dummy, allowing the captain to fire Arsenal ahead.



There were plenty who felt Arsenal should have added another superstar attacker before the window shut.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Havertz scoring, Tzolis helping create the winner and Konsa impressing on his first start made this about as good an afternoon as Arteta could have hoped for.

Three points on the pitch and perhaps a few points proved off it too.

Sports.title: Birmingham star breaks down in tears in emotional live TV interview about owner Tom Wagner’s health battle
Sports.content:
BIRMINGHAM forward Jay Stansfield broke down in tears while discussing the club owner’s health during a television interview.

American businessman Tom Wagner spearheaded a takeover of the West Midlands outfit three years ago alongside NFL legend Tom Brady.

But the 57-year-old sparked fears at the club when he had to be rushed to the hospital after suffering a stroke in February.



He was told to steer clear of the Blues’ games during his recovery, but he was finally able to make his return for their 2-2 draw with Wolves on Sunday.



He was given a raucous reception from the fans, and that love was clearly also felt on the pitch as Stansfield gave an emotional response when asked about the homecoming.

The teary-eyed striker said after the match: “Yeah it’s special.

“I’ve been in contact with him (Wagner) the last few weeks so to have him here is special.”

Stansfield reckoned he could feel the difference Wagner made as the side came from behind twice to take a point, adding: “He gave us a big boost today.”

Wagner made his money as the co-founder of investment firm Knighthead Capital Management.

He bought into Birmingham in the summer of 2023, with Brady investing in the side as a minority owner the following month.



The club suffered relegation to League One in the pair’s first season in charge, but bounced straight back the following year.

Their rise was documented in an Amazon Prime docu-series about the club, called Built In Birmingham: Brady & The Blues.

Alongside their new Hollywood billing, Birmingham have also experienced a boost in financing – with Stansfield smashing the record for the most expensive League One arrival ever when he signed from Fulham for a fee of £15million in 2024.

In fact, all three of the top most expensive arrivals to the British third tier were signed by Birmingham in that 2024/25 window, with Christoph Klarer and Willum Willumson arriving for around £3.5m each.



It’s not hard to see why Wagner is such a beloved figure at the club, although they have endured a mediocre start to the campaign in which they have drawn four of their five matches.

They might have more good news on the horizon though as Wagner continues to drive forward plans to build a new 62,000-seater stadium in the city.

David Raya – 7

Grew into the game and made a couple of huge tackles and blocks as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. Partnership with Konsa will take time to develop, but there were some green shoots here. Led the backline well.

As always, the Italian caused chaos by cropping up in some dangerous attacking positions. Had an early goal ruled out for offside. Arsenal’s left flank is a different beast when Calafiori is fit and firing.

Playing a deeper role this season, so much so that his nickname of ‘The Horse’ may have to be changed. Still having a big influence on games, though, and led from the middle of the park.

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Steadfast Wes Fofana holds his ground despite Arsenal scoring twice as Cole Palmer bullied out of game
Sports.content:
CHELSEA suffered their first Premier League defeat of the season as Arsenal came from behind to win 2-1 at the Emirates.

Morgan Rogers handed Xabi Alonso’s side a dream start by firing the Blues ahead after just 77 seconds.



But former Chelsea star Kai Havertz hit back before half-time to drag the champions level.

And Martin Odegaard completed the turnaround after the break to condemn Chelsea to derby defeat.



SunSport’s Dan King gives his verdict on the Chelsea XI…

EMI MARTINEZ – 5

Took a kick in the head, made two good saves then failed badly to stop Havertz’s equaliser in an eventful first half. Excellent second-half stop from Bukayo Saka to keep his team in a game which was running away from them.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 5

Acquitted himself pretty well in first half but let Tzolis come inside too easily in move for Arsenal’s second goal. Kept his head up, though, and dug in to help prevent Arsenal grabbing a third. Will keep improving.

MAXENCE LACROIX – 5

Poor first touch early on and often looked hesitant and slow as Arsenal poured forward. Is yet to bring his Crystal Palace form to his new club. The Blues missed Levi Colwill’s presence and passing.

WESLEY FOFANA – 7

Commanding first-half performance of blocks, headers and tackles to keep the Gunners at bay. Undone by a brilliant Havertz dummy for Arsenal’s second but still his team’s most consistent performer across the game..



PEDRO NETO – 6

Mostly sound defensively. Offered a good outlet out wide, only to be guilty of poor crosses, although he did hit the post with decent first-half effort. Lacking in end product in second half, too, but OK overall.

ROMEO LAVIA – 6

Looked good in the first half – strong, confident (sometimes a bit too much) and snapped into tackles to stop Chelsea being pinned back. Upset to be taken off on the hour but had faded noticeably to hand the initiative to Arsenal.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

REECE JAMES – 7

Did his calm best alongside feisty Lavia to stem home tide as they stood up to Rice and Lewis-Skelly. Tested Raya with a decent shot and came back into the game when Gusto was introduced.

JORREL HATO – 6

Involved in opening goal but otherwise had a lot to do in defence, with mixed results as Arsenal reached the byline frequently. Did keep Bukayo Saka fairly quiet but replaced as hosts took control early in the second half..



COLE PALMER – 4

Contributed little in the first half apart from one shot and penetrating pass, then yellow card for cynical foul on Havertz. Got on ball a bit more in the second half but still could not make things happen.

MORGAN ROGERS – 6

Early volley was not his best, but good enough to beat David Raya. Offered other flashes but another to fade in second half when poor first touch ruined promising break. Frustration after Rice foul led to booking.

JOAO PEDRO – 5

Worked hard as ever, but unable to fashion an opening for himself or others.. Silly first-half booking for kicking the ball away forced him to hold back. Chasing shadows for much of second half.



SUBS

PEP CHAVARRIA (for Hato, 60) – 6

Helped stiffen Chelsea as Arsenal were looking ominously close to a third. Offered a bit more going forward than Hato had, although not all the Dutchman’s fault.

MALO GUSTO (for Lavia, 60) – 6

Immediately had a sight of goal but fired over. Brought some more energy to a midfield which was flagging but not enough to force an equaliser.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

ESTEVAO (for Neto, 81) – 6

Came on as right winger as Blues chased game, and forced a superb save from Raya in the 89th minute. Should have come on earlier.

DANNY WELBECK (for Rogers, 87) – 5

Applauded on to the pitch by Arsenal fans, who will be just as pleased he was unable to make much impact.

Sports.title: Sky Sports cameras reveal what was on note Xabi Alonso sent to Reece James during Arsenal’s win over Chelsea
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO passed a note to Reece James in the crunch moments of Chelsea’s defeat to Arsenal.

And Sky Sports cameras revealed exactly what was on it.



Alonso sent a folded-up piece of paper on with late substitute Danny Welbeck as Chelsea trailed 2-1 at the Emirates.

Blues skipper James was seen analysing it with Cole Palmer in the 88th minute.





One camera angle showed that it was a drawing of a formation on a pitch with three players up front as Chelsea tried to claw themselves level.

The visitors started the match with Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro and Palmer up front – so it was more likely the midfield and defence that Alonso was looking to tweak.

One fan joked on X: “You reckon Alonso just had ‘take [Declan] Rice out’ on that note?”

And another put: “God forbid [Liam] Rosenior hands his players a note during a game. He’s out of his depth. Xabi Alonso just did it.”



Chelsea pushed and probed as the minutes ticked by but left North London licking the wounds of a narrow loss.

They were on course to cause an upset when Rogers – who snubbed Arsenal‘s transfer interest in the summer – volleyed them ahead after just 77 seconds.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But the Gunners kept their cool and equalised midway through the first half when Kai Havertz fired in at the near post.

Havertz then set up what turned out to be the winner from Martin Odegaard – although he will not be credited with the assist.

The pass from the left came from Christos Tzolis – but it was Havertz’s dummy that made the space for Odegaard to slam home.



Fans were treated to a back-and-forth contest that was tense at times, with Rogers and his England team-mate, Declan Rice, almost coming to blows late on.

Sports.title: Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1: Gunners win early Premier League title showdown as Havertz and Odegaard seal huge comeback win
Sports.content:
THEY’RE not just “Set Piece FC” any more.

But they’re still the best in the land, perhaps by a country mile.



And while Xabi Alonso and Chelsea were not humiliated at the Emirates, the gap between champions and early-season pretenders still seems a chasm.

Last term, acclamation for Mikel Arteta’s side came with caveats attached.





Dull to watch. Too controlled and formulaic. Overly reliant on their dead-ball prowess.

Not that any of that mattered when Martin Odegaard raised the Premier League trophy at Selhurst Park in May. Joy and delight were the emotions.

Yet on a September afternoon which showcased how Arteta has released the handbrake and told his team to win AND entertain, the sense that the Gunners are ready to embark on a campaign to attack, rather then merely defend, their crown, was hard to avoid.

For the first time this season – indeed, the first time since the eventually illusory defeat at City in April – Arteta’s team went behind, a punch in the solar plexus from Morgan Rogers, plucked from their grasp by Chelsea’s £117m bid.



Rogers ended battered and baited, sent flying both legitimately by Ezri Konsa and less fairly by Declan Rice, receiving a booking for his protests and the bird from the home fans.

What followed that goal, though, was instructive and enthralling.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Arsenal ratings vs Chelsea: Havertz reminds Blues of what they let go but Lewis-Skelly in second gear KAI HAVERTZ inspired an Arsenal fight-back as they beat London rivals Chelsea to continue their perfect start. The Gunners were chasing the game after their former transfer target, Morgan Rogers, volleyed the visitors ahead after just 77 seconds. But Arsenal kept their cool and equalised when Havertz fired inside the near post midway through the first half. Havertz then set up Arsenal’s second – even though he won’t get credited with the assist – as his excellent dummy created the space for Martin Odegaard to turn in from close range. Chelsea gave Havertz his break in Premier League football when they shelled out big money to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen in 2020. But he has enjoyed tormenting them – scoring four goals in seven head-to-heads – since he moved across the capital three years later. Here is the verdict of SunSport’s Simon Collings on how each Arsenal player performed…

Vibrant attacking football, swift passing, intensity and conviction, to end with the Arsenal only trailing Enzo Maresca’s new team at the summit on goals scored after three straight wins.

And in the crucial moments, poise and certainty when they had to pull the trigger.



Kai Havertz, a bundle of invention, deservedly pulled them level – although Emi Martinez will not be alone in reflecting that he might have done better – fitting reward for their determination to get back on the front foot.

And when Odegaard ghosted through a gap the width of the Channel Tunnel – created by Havertz’ gorgeous sleight of foot which left Wesley Fofana a befuddled mess – to fire home five minutes into the second half, it never really looked as if Chelsea would find a way to get back on terms.

That is not to dismiss the industry of Alonso’s side.

They will be fantastic going forward, lightning on the counter, with Joao Pedro a constant menace – as he showed by winning the free-kick that led to that early opener.

Rogers’ volley was top drawer – although the bout of head tennis that preceded it was less glorious – Cole Palmer had his moments, Pedro Neto hit the post just before the interval.



Joao Pedro gave Ezri Konsa a tough full debut, especially in the opening 45 minutes.

Yet they are defensively vulnerable, far too vulnerable to be realistic challengers for the title.

Three games played, seven goals conceded. Eight scored, yes, but you can’t keep on playing a high-wire act without falling off now and again.

And the fall could have been harder and faster, too, had Arsenal taken all the opportunities their fluency and invention carved out.

Arteta will recognise this was a proper test, especially after Chelsea went ahead so early, when Arsenal failed to deal with Reece James’ free-kick and Rogers sent his 20-yarder past the slow-reacting David Raya.



But one his side passed, with flying colours, taking the reins and pushing Chelsea deeper and deeper, forcing errors until, eventually, the Blue dam broke.

Alonso’s response to Arsenal’s corner threat – sending four players towards the halk-way line to prevent the red shirts flooding the box – did work.

They were far less convincing as inventive free-kicks, first from Odegaard, then from Declan Rice, should have brought parity.

Riccardo Calafiori’s air-shot squandered the initial opening – Gabriel was lucky to avoid sanction for a stray into Martinez’ head.



Chelsea ratings vs Arsenal: Fofana holds his ground against Arsenal but Palmer is bullied out of game CHELSEA suffered their first Premier League defeat of the season as Arsenal came from behind to win 2-1 at the Emirates. Morgan Rogers handed Xabi Alonso’s side a dream start by firing the Blues ahead after just 77 seconds. But former Chelsea star Kai Havertz hit back before half-time to drag the champions level. And Martin Odegaard completed the turnaround after the break to condemn Chelsea to derby defeat. SunSport’s Dan King gives his verdict on the Chelsea XI…

Then when the Italian did convert from the next one, scrambling home, VAR rightly spotted Konsa was clearly offside when he hit the post in the build-up.

But it was delaying the inevitable and – after moments of danger at the other end involving James, Palmer and Joao Pedro – Arsenal were on terms.

Havertz, his movement outstanding, received from Rice, wide on the right.

It should have been dealt with but he was able to float in unchallenged, Maxence Lacroix the final man in dereliction, before squeezing between Martinez and his left-hand upright. The keeper should have done better.



Chelsea responded, Rogers wide from 16 yards after linking with Joao Pedro, before the half ended with Neto, scampering down the right and seeing his left footer travel beyond Raya but thud against the post.

Yet there was no real answer, until it was far too late, to the decisive moment as Arsenal switched the ball from right to left, Calafiori finding Christos Tzolis.

The Greek played towards Havertz, whose dummy left Fofana a statue as Odegaard ploughed through the gap before smashing past the exposed Martinez. A brilliant goal.

Arsenal were happy to hold what they had, backing Raya to save, gather and punch.



They know they can do that, too.

The Spaniard parried one effort from Palmer and then, two minutes from time, flew high to his right to deny a superb strike from Estevao.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

We’ve seen that movie a few times before.

But the rest of the Arsenal script is different. Much more fun. Unless you have to play them.

Sports.title: 'There are no rules here' - Hamilton criticises Ferrari after Leclerc clash
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has accused Ferrari of having "no rules" after a clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc during the Italian Grand Prix.

Hamilton launched an aggressive move up the inside of his team-mate at the first corner, but was then forced off onto the gravel himself on the exit of the chicane as Leclerc held onto the inside line.

Hamilton dropped from his starting position of fourth to 10th, and was left playing catch-up for the rest of the race, as he eventually finished sixth.

Leclerc held onto third after the incident, which featured contact between the pair, but then crashed out of the race on the second lap, leaving Ferrari to suffer a dismal afternoon at their home race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

"I think it comes down to rules of engagement," said Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025.

"When I was at Mercedes, we had written rules of engagement.

"We never really, really had it too bad. There was a moment between me and Nico [Rosberg] a couple of times, but more often not, it was good.

"Here, there are no rules. We need to address that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc crashes out of the Italian GP

Too late or too early for team orders?

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed a stunning victory from 19th at the grid to extend his advantage over Hamilton to 76 points, while the Ferrari driver also fell 10 points behind George Russell as the Brit completed a Mercedes one-two.

It had been a topic of discussion in the media before the race as to whether Ferrari should prioritise Hamilton over Leclerc given his advantage in the standings, which was extended to 36 points by Sunday's result.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton says the team are 'too late' to implement any sort of 'Ferrari priority'.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 after the race whether he should have priority over Leclerc, Hamilton replied: "We are too far past that already. It's too late for that now.

"I lost a lot of points today to those guys.

"We will do our best to keep pushing the rest of the season but they are out now, out ahead of us."

Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur insisted that it was too early in the season for the team to prioritise one of their drivers.

Vasseur justified his position by using the example of McLaren's experience last year, when Oscar Piastri led Lando Norris in the standings before being hauled in by both his team-mate and Max Verstappen by the end of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok was at the SkyPad to look at who was at fault after Lewis Hamilton went down to 10th position after this contact with Charles Leclerc.

"For sure, the outcome of the first corners is not good for the team," Vasseur said.

"Now, to see if we have a team order or whatever, I think that the good comparison that I made was that last year, Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season and if McLaren put everything on Piastri, Max Verstappen would have been champion.

"For sure, at one stage you have to take a decision but I think it was too early to take a decision before Monza. Now we have time to discuss with the guys."

Leclerc: We went too far

Leclerc admitted that he and Hamilton had gone "too far" in their early battle, but questioned who was "forcing" a narrative playing the team-mates off against each other.

The Monegasque referred to the previous race in Zandvoort when Hamilton had been left frustrated by being held up by Leclerc during the race when the pair were on different strategies.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc explains what caused the Ferrari driver to crash out in the early stages of the Italian Grand Prix.

"I don't really know who is forcing that narrative that we are one against the other," Leclerc said.

"I mean, honestly, Zandvoort, there was way too many talks already.

"Here, it's true though that we went too far. I think Lewis in Turn 1, then Turn 2, I tried to do the tightest corner possible, but that was just not enough - and doing it here is not good."

Should Ferrari have pitted Hamilton?

Hamilton was also once more left frustrated by his team's strategic decisions, with the 41-year-old questioning both the choice of tyre compound for him after the early red flag, and a later decision not to pit him under a virtual safety car.

"It's one of the harder ones to swallow today," he told Sky Sports F1. "I was definitely hoping for more.

"I gave it absolutely everything. We just didn't have the speed on the straights and we were mostly a sitting duck to the guys around me.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg says it is 'not feasible' for Ferrari to favour Lewis Hamilton at this stage of the season.

"We will look internally and try and figure out what we could have done better. I felt we should have been on the hard tyre [on the restart] but we also would have had to overtake people, because we were further back than we were supposed to be.

"I thought they were going to stop us [under the VSC] but they didn't stop us, so I ran out of tyres."

Vasseur said that Ferrari's difficultly overtaking due to a lack of straight-line speed meant they would have struggled to make an extra stop work in the way that Antonelli and Verstappen, who finished third, were able to.

"We were 10 seconds behind Max before the VSC and we finished 10 seconds behind," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1.

"If you do this [pit], you have to overtake and overtaking is not our favourite topic. It would have been more difficult."

Sports.title: Unlucky or unfair? Did Mercedes strategy cost Russell Monza win?
Sports.content:
George Russell feels Mercedes were correct to split strategies despite losing out to Kimi Antonelli in a thrilling Italian Grand Prix.

Russell led Antonelli, who stormed through the field from 19th to be in the lead battle after just 13 laps, by one second when a race-changing Virtual Safety Car was called with 25 laps remaining.

Mercedes pitted Antonelli, but not Russell, for new medium tyres, which put the team-mates 15 seconds apart when the VSC ended.

From sixth, Antonelli overtook his rivals one by one then caught and overtook Russell with three laps to go to win his home event.

It leaves Russell 66 points behind Antonelli in the Drivers' Championship with 10 rounds to go.

"I was on the hard tyre and Kimi was on the medium tyre [when the VSC came], so if either of us were to pit, it was going to be Kimi," said Russell.

"I guess, why I was just a little bit annoyed with the timing of that VSC because, like Max said, I think it would have been tough for those guys on the medium to have competed with anybody on the hard tyre. But, it takes nothing away from Kimi's drive altogether."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The crowd erupted with boos aimed at George Russell as he stepped on Monza podium

Had Mercedes pitted both drivers, Antonelli would have been stuck behind for a few seconds in the pit lane, therefore losing track position to Max Verstappen, who also pitted under the VSC.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The VSC came at an awkward time. I don't think the team knew what the right strategy was and, as Max was in the fight, decided to split the strategy which was probably the right thing for the team to do.

"In hindsight of course, it's easy to say I should have pitted or, if I won the race, they would have said Kimi should have stayed out.

"I would have liked to have had a fight with Kimi. It was quite a nice battle and I felt I was holding my own at that point. That was probably another reason the team wanted us to go on a different strategy. I get it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and George Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix several times

Schiff: I don't know why Russell is not more frustrated Sky Sports F1's Naomi Schiff



I don’t know why he’s not a little bit more frustrated, if I’m totally honest.



"I guess if you’ve given it all and you think that have actually executed the best strategy, and your team-mate has beaten you outright from P19 on the grid, then maybe there is nothing to be frustrated about, other than the fact that Kimi is going to be incredibly tough to beat this season."

Wolff explains Mercedes' thinking at time of VSC

Toto Wolff revealed Mercedes' computer systems told them, at the time of the VSC, that Russell's strategy would be faster than Antonelli's with the Italian expected to "come close but wouldn't catch".

Mercedes believed the hard tyre was a "forever tyre" that would effectively last the whole race, but not with the performance of the medium.

"The differentiator today was the ability going through the traffic [from Antonelli]. We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis [Hamilton] put it in some of the races and that's what he's shown today," said Wolff.

"There's just no stopping when a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell explains why the team chose not to pit him during the VSC, which potentially could have cost him the win in Monza

Coming into the weekend, Antonelli was expected to lose points to his closest title rivals - Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris.

Instead, he's extended his advantage and Russell is set to start at the back himself in one of the upcoming races as he does not have enough engines to finish the season without a grid penalty.

However, Russell says he's "not thinking about" the title race and instead is looking at the positives of being competitive in Monza and Zandvoort compared to the events before the summer break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reflects on his sensational 19th to first Monza victory, catching teammate George Russell to claim a landmark home win and strengthen his championship lead

"We are where we are. Kimi's been driving incredibly this season and deserves to be leading the championship and he's got a healthy lead," he said.

"I'm not going to think about the fight or the comeback. I'm just thinking about going to every race and trying to win it. It will be what it will be. I'm not putting any pressure on myself in this regard, saying 'I need to do this or that'. I just need to win more races and, of course, he's in this spot."

Sports.title: No blockbuster signing but Arsenal's attack still finding another level
Sports.content:
Midway through the second half at the Emirates Stadium, Martin Odegaard picked up the ball in an inside-right position and threaded a pass towards Kai Havertz, whose flick allowed the onrushing Bukayo Saka to test Emiliano Martinez.

The Chelsea goalkeeper managed to push his effort around the post. But the slick passage of play was one of many examples of how the champions, on maximum points after a third straight win, are feeling the benefits of having the trio available again.

Much of the focus ahead of the game had fallen on Chelsea's front three. How would Arsenal contain Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer? It seemed the script had been written when Rogers stunned the ground into silence after 77 seconds.

But Arsenal regained their poise and proved a point about their own attack. Rogers was one of three high-profile forwards to elude them during the summer along with Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. But they may still have the tools to level up without them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Arsenal's 2-1 win over Chelsea

The key is simply to get their best attackers on the pitch, something injuries prevented for much of the last two seasons. This was the first time since December 2024 that Odegaard, Havertz and Saka have started a third straight league game together.

Odegaard and Havertz made the decisive contributions, combining for the winner when the former finished coolly following the latter's dummy. Earlier, Havertz had equalised with his precise finish at Martinez's near post from the edge of the box.

"They have been Arsenal's two best players," said Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville when they were substituted to loud applause. Saka wasn't bad either, tearing into Chelsea on the right and earning a standing ovation of his own later in the second half.

The clamour for Arsenal to add a forward was of course understandable. The club's efforts, although ultimately fruitless, showed they appreciate the need for it. In an ideal world they would have marquee signing leading them into this season.

Image: Martin Odegaard celebrates after scoring Arsenal's second goal

But they can go at least some way to making up the shortfall by keeping Odegaard, Havertz and Saka fit. The last time they managed it over the course of a full season, in 2023/24, they finished the campaign with a club-record 91 Premier League goals.

It helps that Odegaard has rediscovered his scoring touch.

Their captain is unrecognisable from the player who only scored once in 36 games last term. His winner puts him on three in four for the new campaign; his latest another example of how he is getting into the box more. Arteta noted other differences.

"He's fit, and confidence-wise I think it's one of the highest that I've seen him," he said. "He also has a point to prove from last season after missing so much football, and Bukayo the same. We missed so many attacking players last season for long, long periods."

His chemistry with both Saka and Havertz is another factor. They were the two players he passed to most against Chelsea. Odegaard found Saka 10 times and Havertz seven. But his understanding with both, the latter in particular, extends to off-the-ball runs too.

"He's a really smart player and moves so well," Odegaard told Sky Sports of Havertz. "He takes defenders' attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind, I'm always free."

Arteta agreed. "When you start to feel the chemistry they have between them and what they can produce, it's great," he added. "For me, he gets to that point because he's enjoying his football.

Image: Arsenal's Kai Havertz celebrates his goal against Chelsea

"And when you are there, you have to enjoy what you do, you have to play with real intent, and that's what I loved to see from him today. He was running forward, he took shots, he created so many situations for his team-mates, so it was great."

Havertz, also on three goals in four games, has been similarly impactful. This was another all-round performance to underline just how much he gives the side, as an aerial outlet and runner in behind who links with his midfielders and works incessantly.

"To displace Havertz from this team, you need to be one of the best players in the world," said Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

Three Premier League games in, Odegaard, Havertz and Saka account for all six of Arsenal's goals. But the performance against Chelsea showed it has been a collective endeavour too.

As against Coventry and Aston Villa, Arsenal appeared notably more fluid in the final third, with Havertz often pulling to the right, Saka popping up centrally or even swapping flanks with Christos Tzolis, and Riccardo Calafiori appearing everywhere.

"It was another layer," added Arteta to Sky Sports. "Another layer of dynamism, of threat, of intent, of aggression in the attacking phase. You have certainly seen that today."

Chelsea struggled to cope with the level of movement. Even before the second goal, Arsenal had got in behind their backline repeatedly; their combinations, usually in the right half-space, where Odegaard and Saka, in particular, do their best work, proved problematic.

The challenge now is to keep them fit. A spate of injuries like those suffered in the last two seasons might leave fans pining for that blockbuster signing again. But for now they can enjoy what they have. Odegaard, Havertz and Saka are leading their charge.

Sports.title: Sabalenka edges Townsend to reach US Open quarters and retain No 1 spot
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka is clinging on to her US Open title and the world No 1 spot after an unconvincing win over Taylor Townsend.

The Belarussian battled through 6-4 6-3 on Arthur Ashe Stadium in a bizarre match which featured 11 breaks of serve from 19 games.

Sabalenka has spent 99 weeks at the top of the rankings but she needs to win a third straight Flushing Meadows title - and for current No 2 Elena Rybakina to lose before the semi-finals - if she is to reach a century.

Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula are also within striking distance in a four-way battle for the No 1 spot.

"It's super challenging but once again it's important to focus on yourself," said Sabalenka, who had to come from a break down in the second set against popular American Townsend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Taylor Townsend and Naomi Osaka both made a statement with their eye-catching outfits as they took to the court. But who wore it best? You decide...

"I was like 'okay, you are down the break, just try to return the serve and put as much pressure on her as possible'.

"I was just trying to stay focused on myself, not only point by point but ball by ball. I'm happy I was able to turn around the second set, I think it was a key moment."

How did Sabalenka perform?

Sky Sports Tennis' Martina Navratilova:

"It was good enough. It was pretty solid. Townsend had more winners but Aryna did really well returning serve and with passing shots.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A rare sight from Aryna Sabalenka as she completely misses two returns from Taylor Townsend's serve, failing to make contact with the ball on either occasion.

"Townsend tried to come into the net more, but she wasn't successful there, that's how well Sabalenka played from the baseline.

"Overall, I would give Sabalenka a 'B' because she lost her serve so many times, but she played really well when it mattered."

'Showwoman Sabalenka meant business'

Sky Sports Tennis' Annabel Croft:

"There was a lot of ferocious intensity to what Sabalenka brought onto this court. When she went a break down in the second set, she really galvanised herself. When she got back on track, she let out the most enormous shriek and you just knew she meant business.

"The passion, the aura, the mentality, the personality, she brings so much to every court. She's a great showwoman and puts on a show whenever she plays tennis. She understands this isn't just sport, it's entertainment as well.

"She is going to take some beating. She doesn't look as vulnerable as I was expecting. So far, she hasn't dropped a set and looks in very good shape."

Sports.title: Arsenal edge out Chelsea in pulsating London derby
Sports.content:
Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 in the first real major Premier League heavyweight clash of the new campaign - in an early contender for game of the season.

Both London rivals produced a Sunday afternoon treat which rubberstamped Arsenal's credentials as the team to beat - and Chelsea's as worthy challengers for the top honours.

A pulsating game started right from the off as Morgan Rogers - sought after by Arsenal this summer - crashed new club Chelsea ahead after just 77 seconds. That poked the bear of the champions - who produced a response.

Image: Morgan Rogers scored against the club that tried to sign him

After Riccardo Calafiori saw a goal disallowed for offside, former Blue Kai Havertz got his fourth goal against his old club for Arsenal with a strike from the edge of the box.

But despite a dominant Arsenal display, Chelsea still went inches away from a second as Rogers curled wide and Pedro Neto hit the post.

Arsenal turned the tide after the break as Martin Odegaard scored his second goal of the season via a slick team move - which was a carbon copy of the attack that saw him score in the Community Shield against Man City.

And despite some half chances for Chelsea, it was Arsenal who looked more likely to add to their tally - as Emiliano Martinez smartly kept out Bukayo Saka and Ezri Konsa in quick succession. That was until Estevao produced an 89th-minute curler - which needed tipping over by David Raya.

The result means Arsenal stay perfect - level with Manchester City after three games. But Chelsea have shown they will not be far behind...

The key moments from the Emirates

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers gives Chelsea an early lead

77 seconds: GOAL! Rogers fires Chelsea in front from the edge of the box after a free-kick is cleared into his path.

5: SCRAMBLE! Arsenal try to hit back through Odegaard's low free-kick but Calafiori and Gabriel fail to convert from close range amid a goalmouth scramble.

12: GOAL DISALLOWED! Another low free-kick from Declan Rice leads to another scramble and this time Calafiori taps home - but Konsa is flagged in an offside position in the build-up.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Riccardo Calafiori's goal against Chelsea is ruled out by VAR as Ezri Konsa is spotted to be in an offside position!

18: BIG SAVE! Arsenal's onslaught continues as Saka is denied by Martinez down the right wing with a solid stop.

25: GOAL! Havertz beats Martinez at the near post with a drive from the edge of the box.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kai Havertz finds a gap at the near post and levels for Arsenal

31: CLOSE! Rogers nearly has a second but his curling effort from inside the box bends just wide.

45+3: OFF THE POST! Neto strikes the woodwork after another Chelsea breakaway.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pedro Neto hits the post

50: GOAL! Odegaard latches onto Christos Tzolis' pass - via Havertz's smart dummy - to crash in Arsenal's second.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal ahead

61: OVER! Chelsea substitute Malo Gusto curls over a good chance on the edge of the box after being set up by Neto.

69: WHAT A SAVE! Martinez denies Saka from putting Arsenal in control with a fingertip stop.

72: ANOTHER SAVE! Martinez stops Konsa's header from Saka's corner on the goalline.

89: WHAT A SAVE! Estevao's late curler denied by stunning Raya palm over the crossbar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Raya makes an important save from Estevao

Why other teams will be worried about Arsenal

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that William Saliba, - who is genuinely world-class and arguably probably the best centre-back in world football - has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it doesn't look like anyone can score against them.

"There is a massive gulf between both teams - their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today.

"We don't normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They're so strong defensively they don't need to get involved in those games.

"They still didn't look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box."

Arteta: We are capable of being better than last season

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"I think it's an indication for us of how capable we are to perform at an even higher level than last season.

"And it depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humility, and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team. We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer, and this is the ambition of the team.

"I think it was an exceptional performance. I think I enjoyed every minute of it from the beginning to the end, and the beginning was tough, but I enjoyed it because the team reacted in a spectacular way.

"The conviction, the determination, the quality of which I intend to have them constantly, it was beautiful.

"It was a fascinating game, I think, for the spectator as well, and I think we deserved to win the game, which I'm really pleased with, obviously."

Alonso: The number of goals we're conceding is something we need to address

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to Sky Sports:

"My priority is to win games. Normally you win games when you don't concede many goals. It's something we need to address. We need to be tighter, more clinical, more balanced but this takes time.

"We wanted to compete, win here. We knew we were not that far but it went their way. We could have scored for 2-1 and you never know what happens.

"The result is the result; I can't argue against that. But we need to take it, not happy. It hurts. Disappointed for sure. This is our first defeat.

"I want to compete in the best possible way to win. Today we didn't want to sit deep from the first minute. We want to be active, protagonists in the pressing. We have done many right things. We need to make it better, learn from them.

"When you play at the top level, we want to be as efficient in all the phases of the game. But this is where we are. It's game three or four for us in a new phase starting with Chelsea. I'm pleased with the spirit and attitude of the players. They worked hard."

Sports.title: Ødegaard fires winner as Arsenal complete comeback win over Chelsea
Sports.content:
The first heavyweight encounter of the Premier League season was previewed in some quarters as the immovable object versus the irresistible force. Arsenal do not give an inch. Chelsea have been fun and free-scoring under Xabi Alonso. Yet that overlooked something pretty fundamental. The percussive force of Arsenal’s game when they have the ball and want to make something happen.

Chelsea landed a significant blow after 77 seconds when Morgan Rogers put them in front with nicely executed volley from the edge of the area. It was not only the first goal that Arsenal have conceded this season but one with rich narrative strands. Rogers was chased by Arsenal over the summer only to join Chelsea for £117m.

The story here was about Arsenal’s reaction. The sheer fury of it. For a blistering spell that culminated in Kai Havertz’s equaliser on 25 minutes, they threatened to blow Chelsea off the pitch. Arsenal’s confidence shone through. They had not lost to their cross-town rivals in eleven previous meetings in all competitions, winning eight, but it was rooted in more than that. They had too much for Chelsea and they knew it.

Martin Ødegaard’s goal shortly after half-time proved the difference – it followed a stunning feint by Havertz – and it continued Arsenal’s perfect start to their title defence. It is now three wins out of three. They will take some stopping. Then again, everybody already knows this.

It was possible to feel a blast from the past as Alonso lined up with three central defenders. Almost exactly ten years ago, Antonio Conte brought Chelsea here and trailed 3-0 at half-time. Cue the manager’s switch to three at the back, a click and a bolt towards the title. This was the acid test for Alonso and his team could not have made a better start. They had scored very early in Alonso’s first two league matches against Fulham and Brighton and it was the same again.

Arsenal offered £80m to Aston Villa for Rogers but no more. Chelsea went higher, much higher and there was an inevitability about him showing up when it mattered. Arsenal did not clear their lines after a Reece James free-kick and when Jorrel Hato outjumped Ødegaard, the ball broke nicely for Rogers. The volley was threaded into the bottom corner. Could David Raya have done better? It felt that way in the moment.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers is challenged by his former Aston Villa teammate Ezri Konsa. Photograph: Daniel Hambury/EPA

Arsenal’s response was just ferocious. It was the intensity and the physical levels. The Emirates sounded like a bear-pit as the home crowd yelled after what felt like every coming together, every time an Arsenal player tumbled over. The equaliser was extensively trailed and it came when Havertz was allowed to drift along the edge of the Chelsea area from right to left. There was no challenge and his low shot beat Emiliano Martínez inside the near post.

It was a soft concession and out of keeping with the resilience that Chelsea had shown up to that point. Especially Martinez. The former Arsenal goalkeeper had thrown himself into a thicket of legs to keep out a low Ødegaard free-kick delivery, taking a boot to the head by Gabriel Magalhães for his troubles. He also saved brilliantly from the Arsenal centre-half shortly afterwards, keeping him out at close quarters after João Pedro had failed to clear a Declan Rice free-kick. On the rebound, Ezri Konsa hit the post before Riccardo Calafiori lashed the loose ball home. Konsa was found to have been offside and the goal was disallowed.

Arsenal created a staggering number of openings before the Havertz goal. Chelsea put their bodies on the line. Martínez got his angles right to deny Bukayo Saka; Wesley Fofana made a big block to thwart Havertz. After James had worked Raya from distance, Arsenal stormed to the other end and Hato leapt into a saving block on Ødegaard.

It was breathless stuff and it was as if Arsenal exhaled after the equaliser. This kind of tempo is surely unsustainable. Chelsea kicked out a foothold. Rogers curled past the far post and there was the crucial moment just before the interval when João Pedro got Pedro Neto away up the right. He cut inside and steered a low shot against the far post.

Arsenal cleared their heads for the second-half and they were in front almost immediately. Ødegaard started and finished the move but it was all about the dummy from Havertz, who knew where his captain was when Christos Tzolis sent over a low ball from the left. Havertz’s move froze Fofana and Ødegaard had the freedom of the Chelsea area to finish. A couple of words about Tzolis: very polished.

Arsenal were not afraid to go long and fast from back to front through Raya; the challenges were numerous for Chelsea. They looked to their big guns to mount the fightback. Rogers almost got away only to be halted by a thunderous Konsa slide challenge. Cole Palmer flitted around the edges. He had a couple of half chances.

Saka forced Martínez into a fine save after a lovely touch from Havertz and Arsenal almost scored again from a corner, Martínez grabbing a loose ball when he was already on the ground. Chelsea pushed in the closing stages and they could point to the moment on 89 minutes when Estêvão, on as a substitute, exploded a drive from the edge of the area and watched Raya tip over. Arsenal did not deserve to drop points.

Sports.title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw
Sports.content:
David Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind to salvage a point against Manchester United through Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.

The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.

Tyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.

The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.

“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.

“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”

Moyes also paid tribute to the quality of the goals from Maitland-Niles and George, who cancelled out finishes from Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko respectively.

“If nobody knew you that goal would get you plenty of headlines,” he said of Maitland-Niles, a £4.3m deadline-day signing from Lyon. “It was a brilliant goal, brilliant technique. We have not had a chance to get to know Ainsley but it was a great start from him.”

Sports.title: Embattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-election
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election next year despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.

Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. The 56-year-old Swiss is under severe pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in Fifa tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors.

Uefa, the European governing body, has led calls for Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

But for the first time since the plan became public, Fifa has reiterated Infantino’s intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year’s elections. Should he be re-elected, he will continue to serve as head of world football until 2031.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino. Montagliani, a Fifa vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed Fifa’s purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss.

However, Infantino is not without friends – Saudi Arabia, the 2034 men’s World Cup hosts, came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body, Caf, and South America’s Conmebol also supportive.

As the only declared candidate so far for the election due to take place in March 2027, Infantino will need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to Fifa to extend his term of office, which began in 2016. Candidate nominations for next year’s election must be submitted by 18 November.

Sports.title: Armstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves draw
Sports.content:
If only Adam Armstrong, the Wolves striker presented with a golden chance in the 87th minute, had shot into the same corner of the net at the Railway End that his teammate ­Jackson Tchatchoua had located when scoring one of the most ­memorable own goals at the end of the first half, then César Peixoto’s team would surely now be second in the Championship.

Instead Armstrong, one of the Football League’s most proven goalscorers, lifted his shot over an open goal from 10 yards when played in by Fer López at the end of this implausibly open derby. Birmingham ultimately deserved to extend their unbeaten start to the league season.

After their 4-2 defeat at West Ham on Tuesday, Wolves look as vulnerable defensively as they can be devas­tating going forward. Only Burnley, relegated with them last season, have conceded more than their 10 goals.

Tom Wagner, the ­Birmingham chair, was back in the St Andrew’s directors’ box for the first time since a stroke in February and was treated to a thrilling game. Spoils were shared but Chris Davies was happy with his side after they twice came from behind. “I’ll always be content when the players put in that heart and spirit,” the ­Birmingham manager said. “When you look at the quality of their team, I’ll be astonished if they’re not in the top four. Second half, we put them to the sword.”

López scored in the third ­minute for Wolves and, after Jay ­Stansfield equalised in controversial circum­stances, Ladislav Krejci gave the visitors the lead again. But then came the moment that could haunt ­Tchatchoua. The Cameroon right‑back was under no pressure as he went to turn a long diagonal from Phil Neumann back towards his ­goalkeeper – but instead looped the ball wide and over José Sá into his own goal.

That moment set the tempo for the rest of a game. Wolves, despite ­retaining the majority of their ­Premier League squad after the transfer deadline, know sheer quality of player alone will not mean promotion.

Peixoto called for video assistant referees to be brought in to the Championship after Stansfield appeared to handle when bringing down Patrick Roberts’s brilliant chip before hammering home Birmingham’s first equaliser. “If the referee doesn’t see it, then what can you do?” Stansfield said.

Peixoto said: “I don’t know why they don’t have VAR in the Champion­ship. It’s very important to help the refe­rees to take the best decisions. I saw a handball and in the screen we saw a handball.” The ­Portuguese coach also confirmed that in a pre‑season meeting with Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL), ­managers were told that grappling at corners would be penalised. “But it’s not happening,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Adam Armstrong (left) reacts to his missed chance to win it for Wolves at Birmingham. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

While the home side dominated the second half, Wolves could have put the game to bed before Birmingham got going. López was involved in the buildup before advancing to side‑foot home Rodrigo Gomes’s right‑wing cross to the near post for his third goal of the season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Then in the 19th minute, ­Christoph Klarer’s poor touch invited Raúl ­Jiménez to steal the ball and put in Gomes who allowed James ­Beadle to save his dinked attempt.

Krejci is one of the elite players surprisingly still at Wolves. The Czechia captain’s bullet header, after André flicked on Hugo Bueno’s corner, gave Wolves another endorphin boost. It was short-lived, however, as Tchatchoua lobbed home his tragicomic own goal. Jiménez hit the crossbar, as he did in defeat at West Ham, but then Neumann headed against the same woodwork midway through the second half.

Wolves had the clearest of many chances both teams had to win the game. López dispossessed Demarai Gray inside the area and, faced with the goalkeeper, squared for ­Armstrong. Somehow he contrived to lift the ball over the empty goal. “The way Jack[son Tchatchoua] committed his mistake, Adam committed the mistake in the opposite side,” Peixoto said. “We have to take the confidence to them and keep fighting and work hard for the next game.”

There was still time for ­Birmingham to think they had won it as Marvin Ducksch arced a free-kick towards the top corner. There, however, was Sá to show why he was awarded a new contract, as he tipped the ball aside to ensure this pulsating match finished even.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning start
Sports.content:
Some things just feel inevitable. Some strikers just feel inevitable. Despite a new season, a fresh start and new opponents, it is still the same storyline for Manchester City: Khadija Shaw wins them the game. The Jamaica striker began the new campaign exactly how she finished the last league season, with two goals, and demonstrated why it was so crucial that the club eventually persuaded her to sign a new contract in the summer.

The Golden Boot winner in the Women’s Super League could have scored at least twice in the first half, had it not been for an excellent debut performance from newly promoted Birmingham’s new goalkeeper, Sophie Baggaley.

Shaw, though, was not to be denied and she rose highest to head in twice from second-half corners, firstly taken by Kerstin Caspari and then by the debutant Beth Mead, to score her side’s second and third goals in a 3-1 victory. By then, Mary Fowler’s low finish had already opened the scoring, with what was Manchester City’s 1,000th goal as a professional women’s side.

Birmingham grabbed a late consolation through Océane Hurtré, who capitalised on a defensive lapse from Jade Rose and rolled the ball home in the 90th minute, and there were plenty of encouraging signs overall for the second-tier champions of last season. Birmingham were playing on the same ground on which their relegation in 2022 on a night when they were hit for six by Manchester City, but on Sunday Amy Merricks’s side look far stronger and more competitive than the Birmingham team that say goodbye to the top tier four, having kept the scoreline goalless until after half-time.

Nonetheless, on the day of Lauren Hemp’s 200th Manchester City appearance and the club’s 1,000th goal it was a dominant start from the defending champions whose head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, said: “We created a lot of scoring chances. The first half, [we were] a little bit hesitant on the ball, not determined with or without the ball, but the second half was better.”

View image in fullscreen Arsenal's Lisa Baum fires in the only goal at Brighton. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Merricks, who hailed Baggaley’s debut as “exceptional”, said: “We got into some good areas and lacked just a bit of anticipation that we would get there. That’s just down to belief, that’s not quality. I’m really pleased with the performance. I’m disappointed with the result but really pleased with the platform we’ve given ourselves to build on.”

Earlier, Lisa Baum marked her Arsenal debut with an exquisitely taken goal and her early strike was enough to secure a 1-0 victory at Brighton and inflict a defeat on their new head coach, Arturo Ruiz. The 19-year-old Germany youth international created room for herself to shoot inside the area in the 10th minute and rifled home a clinical finish from a tight angle, in off the underside of the crossbar, to make an immediate impression on the delighted, travelling Arsenal fans behind that goal.

Baum, who arrived this summer from RB Leipzig, was one of four new signings to start the game for Arsenal, who also introduced Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodriguez. Arsenal had failed to win at Brighton in the past two league campaigns and will have been very satisfied to open their title bid with a victory as they seek to hunt down a first league title since 2019. Ruiz, who has been in charge for Brighton at nine days, saw some encouraging signs from his new team with Kiko Seike and Fran Kirby both going close.
