It was a day for important debut goals as Lexi Lloyd-Smith slotted home on her first appearance for Crystal Palace to give the promoted side a priceless 1-0 win against Everton to start their campaign. Another debutant quickly impressed at Tottenham as their new striker Kirsty Hanson scored twice to help them to beat West Ham 3-1.

Liverpool were the day’s most emphatic winners as they cruised to a 4-0 victory away at the promoted Charlton. The Germany striker Vivien Endemann scored on her debut for Liverpool after Grace Fisk had scored twice. Cornelia Kapocs added a stoppage-time penalty to make it a poor start for Charlton, who did not register a shot on target and recorded just two efforts off target.

Sports.title: European football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of Valencia
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.

The reigning champions moved three points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.

Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering visitors on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.

Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium.

“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick. “We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us. Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”

Lamine Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Fermín dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star.

The 19-year-old slammed home at the near post for what he thought was Barca’s second goal but the goal was disallowed for a tight offside after a VAR review. Fermín netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up.

Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric García had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with team-mate Rodri’s shoulder, on the midfielder’s first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City.

Lamine Yamal fired narrowly wide and Fermín struck the post as Flick’s side continued to dominate. Barca goalkeeper Joan García made a smart save to thwart Arnaut Danjuma at his near post before the break.

Raphinha, starting again as the team’s centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Fermín fed him.

Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona’s fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo. New arrival Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barca debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide.

Lamine Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barca’s fifth. “We have a very young team, with the right transfers we made, but it’s the beginning of the season, it’s not the end,” added Flick, telling his team not to get too excited yet about their strong start. “We have to go a long, long way.”

Meanwhile, Ronald Koeman Jr, the goalkeeper son of former Netherlands player and manager Ronald Koeman, scored two penalties for Dutch side Telstar to rescue a point in their Eredivisie match with Cambuur. His second spot-kick was converted in the 11th minute of added time.

Koeman Jr, 31, converted his first penalty on 63 minutes before his ice-cool equaliser. He previously scored from the spot at the end of last season to ensure his side avoided relegation from the Dutch top-flight.

View image in fullscreen Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr is hugged by a team-mate after his late penalty rescued a point. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

In Germany, Mainz ignited their Bundesliga season with a thumping 5-0 win over hapless Hamburg, while Augsburg climbed ⁠to the top of the table following a 4-1 win at Eintracht Frankfurt on Sunday.

Mainz had lost 4-0 at Hamburg last season, ⁠but this time round ⁠were in ​complete control from the start and took the lead on 19 minutes as Sheraldo Becker was played in on goal by ⁠Kaishu Sano and picked out the bottom corner. Becker then turned provider as his low cross was converted at the back post by Phillipp Mwene for ⁠a 2-0 halftime lead.

Becker was again involved with the next goal as he set up ​Phillip Tietz to bundle the ball home. Tietz ‌then added a fourth ‌as he beat goalkeeper Heuer Fernandes, before ex-Hamburg player Ransford-Yeboah Koenigsdoerffer punished his former employers ‌with a fifth.

Hamburg sit bottom of the Bundesliga table having lost their opening two matches and have yet to score, while Mainz are in fifth place.

View image in fullscreen Augsburg’s Robin Fellhauer (right) celebrates his goal against Eintracht Frankfurt with team-mate Marius Wolf. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

Augsburg have a full haul of six points following ​their excellent win at Frankfurt, where they had to come from behind having trailed 1-0 at halftime. Jonathan Burkardt headed the home side in front inside six minutes from Younes Ebnoutalib’s lofted pass into the box as Frankfurt dominated the chances and might have been out of sight ⁠by the break.

But it was a totally different affair in the second ​period as Arijon Ibrahimovic ​headed in at the back post ​on debut inside the first minute of the re-start. Within a minute ​of that goal, ‌Augsburg were 2-1 ahead ​as the ball ​fell to Robin Fellhauer in the box and he converted to turn the game on its head. The visitors made it 3-1 when Alexis Claude-Maurice fired in from the edge of the box and Fabian Rieder added a late fourth from a free-kick to complete a comprehensive win.

Augsburg lead the Bundesliga on goal difference ahead of Freiburg, Borussia Dortmund and new boys Elvesberg, who all have two wins from two. Bayern Munich dropped points with a goalless draw at Schalke on Saturday.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglers
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy has returned to English football after signing for Burnley in the Championship as a free agent.

Vardy, who will be 40 in January, has signed a contract until the end of the season, having spent last season at Cremonese in Italy. A return to Leicester, where he spent 13 years and was a Premier League champion in 2016 and an FA Cup winner in 2021, was mooted in the summer, only for Vardy to rule out a reunion.

His podcast, Jamie Vardy’s Having A Party, made the news last week for Mike Dean’s lifting of the lid on his antics as a Premier League referee and has secured broadcast rights for a Bundesliga watch-along. He has also, with his wife Rebekah, starred in an ITV reality series, and been the subject of a Netflix documentary.

Despite those wider interests, Vardy’s intention has been to carry on playing, having been a late starter, making his Football League debut at 25 after signing for Leicester.

Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last term and, with Nicky Hayen as their manager, remain without a win after their opening five games of the Championship campaign, losing to Bristol City on Saturday. Vardy joins a team bottom of the division.

“This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town,” Vardy said. “I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

In June, he said of Leicester, now in League One, currently struggling under the management of Russell Martin: “I think that’s gone. I’ll always support them, always follow them. I think that’s the best thing I can do now.”

Sports.title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.

Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.

“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”

Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”

The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. The Spurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”

No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since five-year driving ban... as loyalties with Kai Trump torn after Vanessa's public show
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since five-year driving ban... as loyalties with Kai Trump torn after Vanessa's public show

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tiger Woods was spotted all smiles on the sidelines at Stanford Stadium on Friday night, making his first public appearance after being hit with a five-year driving ban.

The 15-time major champion returned to his alma mater for the Cardinal's college football clash against the Miami Hurricanes, days after his courtroom appearance.

Sporting a white Stanford cap and a wool quarter zip from his own brand 'Sun Day Red,' Woods was seen laughing and chatting with staffers on the sidelines.

He appeared relaxed and upbeat as he soaked in the action and was also seen in conversation with West Coast rap icon E-40 before the action got underway.

However, the matchup presented an awkward clash of loyalties for the golf legend.

While Woods remains one of Stanford's most celebrated alumni – having won 11 collegiate tournaments before turning pro – his personal ties now run deep in Miami, given his relationship with Vanessa Trump.

Tiger Woods was spotted on the sidelines at Stanford Stadium on Friday night

The 15-time major champion returned to his alma mater for the Cardinal's college football clash

It marked his first public appearance after being hit with a five-year driving ban

Vanessa's 19-year-old daughter, Kai Trump, recently moved to South Florida to begin her freshman year as a collegiate golfer for the University of Miami.

The granddaughter of Donald Trump has regularly documented her move on social media, sharing snaps in Hurricanes gear as she begins her collegiate golf career.

On Friday night, it was Kai's new school that walked away with all the bragging rights, as Miami blew out Woods' beloved Stanford Cardinal in a 45-6 rout.

The outing marked a stark change of scenery from Wednesday morning, when Woods appeared alongside Vanessa to resolve his criminal case stemming from a March 27 crash near his Jupiter Island estate.

Woods' girlfriend held hands with him at the Martin County Courthouse in a show of public solidarity as he finalized his plea deal over a March rollover crash.

Woods pleaded no contest to a reduced charge of reckless driving and refusal to submit to testing, avoiding jail time after entering a plea agreement.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

President Trump declared Woods's plea deal 'very fair' as he weighed in on the matter, just one day after the golf legend discovered his fate from the ordeal.

He added: 'But I think he's going to have somebody drive him. I told him that a long time ago: 'Why don't you get somebody to drive you'

'So he's going to have somebody drive him from now on. He's just a very special guy and I'm glad that was resolved.'

Trump added: 'It's a very tough situation because they didn't find alcohol on him. You know, he didn't test positive at all for alcohol. It's a tough deal when you're taking a painkiller because you're under pain... and you have a problem and you test positive.'

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

Sports.title: 'I don't race dirty': Lewis Hamilton demands Ferrari set out 'rules of engagement' after angrily accusing team-mate Charles Leclerc of pushing him off the track in embarrassing home Grand Prix for Italian team
Sports.content:
'I don't race dirty': Lewis Hamilton demands Ferrari set out 'rules of engagement' after angrily accusing team-mate Charles Leclerc of pushing him off the track in embarrassing home Grand Prix for Italian team

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lewis Hamilton called on Ferrari to issue rules of engagement after the home team’s Italian Grand Prix ended in embarrassment and acrimony.

The seven-time world champion finished sixth after a first-chicane altercation with his team-mate Charles Leclerc, who then crashed out in a 160mph smash that saw him taken to the medical centre, where he was declared ‘OK’.

After going wheel-to-wheel with the Monegasque, he came on to the radio to say, quite rightly: ‘Charles pushed me off.’

Hamilton got as high as third place at various stages yesterday, eliciting huge cheers from the partisan crowd, before dropping back on fading tyres. But it was the management of the two drivers rather than any strategy complaints that was top of his agenda at the end of the race won by Mercedes’ wonderkid Kimi Antonelli.

In a message to team principal Fred Vasseur, the seven-time world champion said: ‘Here there are no rules. And that’s something that needs to change. When I was at Mercedes we had written rules of engagement. And we never had it too bad.

‘There was a moment with me and Nico a couple of times. But more often than not, it was good. Here there are no rules.

Lewis Hamilton was furious when he was pushed off the track during the opening lap

The two Ferraris make contact with Hamilton (left) being squeezed out by his team-mate

Footage from Leclerc's car showed the two coming together, with Hamilton forced off

‘I don’t race dirty. I’ve always raced clean, and fairly, and always left space. So I don’t think they should be worried about me. I’ve come into the team and tried to be respectful of space. And definitely not to put the team in jeopardy. And I stand by that.

‘That’s all I can talk about on my side. You’d have to speak to Fred about the other side and decisions taken there.’

The next round, the 14th of 23, comes next Sunday in Madrid in the city’s first staging of the Spanish Grand Prix.

Hamilton, who fell 76 points behind leader Antonelli, reflected on his dreams of an eighth world title, saying: ‘It’s never over until it is over. With the pace Mercedes have, it’s a very difficult amount to close.’

‘We didn’t do so well today, but it’s painful to badger my guys. They go home to their families. And they are working really hard.

‘But it isn’t good enough. We’ll go back to the drawing table.’

Sports.title: US Open fans mock Naomi Osaka's latest bizarre outfit as Japanese star squeezes through in New York thriller
Sports.content:
US Open fans mock Naomi Osaka's latest bizarre outfit as Japanese star squeezes through in New York thriller

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka wore a different outfit to walk onto Louis Armstrong at the US Open for a third time this tournament on Saturday night, but it did not go down well with fans at home.

Osaka has become known for her bold fashion choices at grand slams in recent years and her outfits in New York this week have been no different.

She stepped out in an all-white ensemble on Thursday, including a long overshirt featuring tennis rackets stitched into the design.

The long tail flowed behind her as she walked onto the court, tripping on the fabric beneath her feet as she walked to the net for the coin toss and to shake hands with her opponent.

The white for the day-time session was a complete contrast to Monday's all-black skirt and tank top promo in the night session on Arthur Ashe.

But Saturday's outfit was completely different again as the Japanese star wore a light-gray zip-up hoodie underneath a tailored gray plaid blazer. On the bottom, Osaka wore a very wide-leg, flowing pair of gray trousers.

Naomi Osaka wore a different outfit to walk onto court at the US Open for a third time

Tthe Japanese star wore a light-gray zip-up hoodie underneath a tailored gray plaid blazer

Osaka then wore an all-black Nike outfit to play in against Elise Mertens on Louis Armstrong

The look did not impress everybody, however, and fans took to social media to give their opinions.

'Nobody cares, it's a tennis court not Paris fashion week ffs,' one commented.

Another posted: 'She's the only one that does this.'

A third responded: 'Always cringe. My favorite tennis player is whoever is playing against Naomi Osaka.

One fan declared Osaka 'looked like a clown', while another insisted they were 'so tired of this'.

The 13th-seeded Osaka progressed to the fourth round by defeating Elise Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5, in a match that lasted two hours, 38 minutes.

The two-time champion put her head on her racket after the final point, stunned at herself at the victory.

'Honestly, I can´t believe I won this match,' Osaka said. 'I´m literally shocked that I won this match.'

Osaka was down 4-2 in the third set and apologized for expressing so much frustration throughout a tough night.

'There was a certain point, I don´t know, I felt like I put my entire heart on the court and then I just kept trying every single point,' Osaka said.

'I didn´t feel like I played amazing, and it was really getting me down. I was very negative on myself.'

Join the discussion Should athletes focus on performance or is making a fashion statement just as important at big events?

The 13th-seeded Osaka progressed to the fourth round by defeating Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5

Earlier in the week, Naomi Osaka was forced to wait until the chair umpire had chided a group of spectators in one of Arthur Ashe's hospitality suites.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

Elsewhere in the stands, another spectator was heard calling out: 'The players are ready!'

When the stadium had stilled somewhat, Osaka returned to her serve but struggled with her ball toss, apologizing as she reset.

Footage captured from another spectator of the group on social media later showed them posing as a group, allegedly during a game, with a person who appeared to be a member of US Open staff holding up a portable light to help them capture the shot.

The social media clip showed another spectator on the same evening posing in front of the court with a portable light, also allegedly during live matchplay.

When contacted by Daily Mail Sport for comment on the incident, Brendan McIntyre, head of US Open communications, said: 'We want our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend the US Open, but we also need to ensure that does not interfere with the action and competition on the court.

'These instances happen infrequently, and similar to when crowd noise reaches a certain level, our chair umpires have the ability to address the crowd when they occur.'

Sports.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea PLAYER RATINGS: Who 'controlled the game' for the Gunners? Which player played 'a big part' in the hosts' win? And who do Chelsea need 'more magic in these massive matches' from?
Sports.content:
Arsenal have made an early statement in the season after beating Chelsea 2-1 in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon. The Gunners fell behind to an early Morgan Rogers strike but battled back through Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard. Daily Mail Sport's ISAAN KHAN (Arsenal) and KIERAN GILL (Chelsea) ran the rule over the players. ARSENAL (4-2-3-1) David Raya – 7 Had to be alert with Chelsea so dangerous on the counter-attack. Goalframe struck by Pedro Neto in the first period. Top save to deny Estevao on 89 minutes. David Raya made a fantastic save late in the second half to prevent Estevao from equalising Ben White – 6.5 Good intricate passes on the right flank which caused problems for the opposition. Hard to control. Ezri Konsa – 6.5 Hit a post in an early scramble in the box. Caught out at times on Chelsea on breakaways. Getting used to his team-mate Gabriel. Gabriel – 7 Kicked Emi Martinez's face in the area when going for the ball early on. A physical display and kept going. Riccardo Calafiori – 7 Thought he scored on 12 mins after bundling the ball home - but Konsa was offside. His unorthodox positioning is very hard to keep tabs on. Riccardo Calafiori, left, produced another solid display at left back for Arsenal on Sunday Declan Rice – 7.5 Such an engine to keep going from one box to the other in a frantic game. Harried the opposition and set the tone. Myles Lewis-Skelly – 7 Calm in receiving the ball in tight spaces. Kept looking to get the ball forward when in possession. Bukayo Saka – 7.5 A constant threat. Drove forward with real venom. Utilised his ability of either going straight towards goal or heading to the byline to cross. Martin Odegaard – 8.5 Controlled the game for Arsenal and struck with a goal, too. Leader's display. Clever free-kick across the floor on five minutes nearly caught Chelsea out. Martin Odegaard scored the winning goal with this strike early on in the second half Christos Tzolis – 8 Executed multiple accurate, low crosses into the area which Arsenal should have profited more from. A handful to deal with. Kai Havertz – 8 After a few tame shots, his goal to equalise was a proper striker's finish. A number of his intricate flick-ons led to chances. Played a big part. SUBS Piero Hincapie – 6.5 Got stuck in and kept looking to lay down a mark in his tackles. Martin Zubimendi – 6.5 Good defensive coverage. Snapped at the heels of the opposition. Viktor Gyokeres – N/A Mikel Merino – N/A SUBS NOT USED: Kepa Arrizabalaga, Bruno Guimaraes, Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze MANAGER: Mikel Arteta – 7.5 His team dominated throughout. Scoreline could've been wider on another day. CHELSEA (4-2-3-1) Emiliano Martinez – 5.5 Welcomed to the Emirates with a kick to the head from Gabriel. Had Robert Sanchez conceded Kai Havertz's equaliser, he'd have been slaughtered by his critics. No stopping Martin Odegaard when through. Emiliano Martinez suffered a blow to the face during a difficult return back to the Emirates Josh Acheampong – 6 Had help from Pedro Neto, who was dropping deep to provide extra protection on the right-hand side. Chelsea's academy graduate tried and failed to stop Christos Tzolis from moving inside for Arsenal's second goal. Wesley Fofana – 5 Havertz's dummy from Tzolis's pass inside totally fooled Fofana as the ball rolled on to Martin Odegaard, with the unmarked Arsenal captain making it 2-1 with only Martinez to beat. Maxence Lacroix – 5.5 Havertz's crack for 1-1 crept through his legs before beating Martinez. Someday Chelsea might keep a clean sheet. But they still need to do a great deal of tightening up at the back first. Jorrel Hato – 5.5 Often tasked with trying to tie down Bukayo Saka. Sometimes the only solution was to foul him. One such free-kick led to Arsenal scoring – but the offside flag saved Chelsea that time. Jorrel Hato, right, endured a difficult afternoon trying to contain the threat of Bukayo Saka Reece James – 6 Swerving strike from 25 yards forced David Raya into a nervy save. Sprayed long passes wide with precision. Captain tried to add control into the centre, but Chelsea continue to resemble chaos. Romeo Lavia – 6 With Moises Caicedo sidelined, Lavia lasted an hour. When replaced by Malo Gusto, Chelsea were left with two right backs manning the midfield. Not ideal for Alonso after losing Enzo Fernandez. Pedro Neto – 6 Lived for counter-attacks, striking the post from one such fast break before half-time. When Arsenal had possession high up the pitch, Chelsea had a back six, with Neto dropping to fill in on the right. Cole Palmer – 5.5 Chelsea need his magic more in these massive matches. Biggest involvement was taking one for the team – a yellow card as he killed an Arsenal counter-attack. Cole Palmer quiet by his standards - in a match that Chelsea needed more from their playmaker Morgan Rogers – 6.5 Arsenal wanted him. Chelsea won him. Then he scored the opener after 77 seconds, a controlled volley from 18 yards giving Mikel Arteta a snapshot of what he could have had. Joao Pedro – 6 Cautioned early on for kicking the ball away ever so slightly – back to that approach now, are we, refs? – and frustrated when fouls on him weren't being called. Lonely job up top at times. SUBS Malo Gusto (for Lavia, 60) – 6 Curled over one chance within seconds of his introduction into the midfield. Pep Chavarria (for Hato, 60) – 6 Hato sprinting up and down the left-hand side was tiring, so Chavarria took over. Estevao Willian (for Neto, 81) – N/A Danny Welbeck (for Rogers, 87) – N/A SUBS NOT USED: Mike Penders, Valentin Barco, Levi Colwill, Jamie Gittens, Geovany Quenda MANAGER: Xabi Alonso – 5.5 Scored early again. Allowed the opposition to pile on the pressure again. Conceded again. Chelsea are craving some control in their games.

Sports.title: England team-mates Morgan Rogers and Declan Rice clash in FURIOUS row during Arsenal's win over Chelsea
Sports.content:
England team-mates Morgan Rogers and Declan Rice clash in FURIOUS row during Arsenal's win over Chelsea

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers came to blows during Arsenal's Premier League victory over Chelsea on Saturday.

Chelsea were trailing when they launched a late attack through Cole Palmer. Arsenal's Rice tripped Rogers just as he was about to sprint into the penalty area, and the visitors' chance of an equaliser went begging as Palmer's effort drifted wide.

Rogers reacted furiously, springing to his feet to shove Rice and wag a finger at his England team-mate while appearing to shout, 'Don't do that', several times, clearly suggesting he felt the challenge had been cynical.

Referee Chris Kavanagh appeared to miss the trip and instead showed the incensed Chelsea midfielder a yellow card for his reaction.

Rogers was taken off shortly afterwards as Xabi Alonso moved to ensure the midfielder did not risk picking up a red card.

Rice went over to his England team-mate after the final whistle had blown to shake his hand, while Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his two players can settle their differences ahead of the Three Lions' Nations League opener against Spain and Czechia at the end of the month.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) September 6, 2026

Arsenal's Rice tripped Rogers just outside the penalty area during a Chelsea attack late on in the two sides' meeting at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday afternoon

Rogers reacted furiously, climbing off the turf and shoving his England team-mate

Rogers had given Chelsea the lead in the second minute with a superb, instinctive goal in the second minute. The Englishman celebrated in front of the Arsenal fans with a Thierry Henry-inspired celebration, with his hand on the corner flag.

Chelsea's dominance was short-lived however. Kai Havertz pulled one back for Arsenal in the 25th minute before Martin Odegaard's 50th-minute winner for the Premier League champions.

The victory ensured Arsenal retain their perfect start to the season, following wins over Coventry City and Aston Villa. They are joined by Manchester City at the top of the table as the only two sides to collect all nine available points from the opening three games.

Meanwhile this was Xabi Alonso's first defeat since taking the reins in west London.

Alonso said: 'The assessment and the feeling (is that) it hurts. It hurts to lose. It hurts to suffer our first defeat. It has been a very intense game, a great fight between two sides who have given everything.

'They have played with the top level of concentration, of intensity. We have tried, we score early, after that Arsenal push us hard and we were struggling a little bit to get control of the ball.

'After the equaliser, it has been quite balanced. We had a couple of chances. It's about details. Once you concede, you need to know it's just one goal. Disappointed that we couldn't take anything from here.'

Sports.title: George Russell's title hopes in tatters as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix to extend his championship lead - despite starting 19th
Sports.content:
George Russell's title hopes in tatters as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix to extend his championship lead - despite starting 19th

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kimi Antonelli galloped from 19th on the grid to win the Italian Grand Prix, all but ending the title hopes of George Russell, who started second and finished second.

‘Exceptionally challenging,’ admitted the Englishman of achieving his career ambition, almost resigned to be a smiling bridesmaid in someone else’s story.

As for Antonelli? What a drive. In triumphing on a strategy that clearly – and controversially – favoured him rather than his Mercedes team-mate Russell, the 20-year-old became the first Italian to win his home race since the black-and-white days of Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

The pivotal moment came on lap 28, when Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin broke down. A virtual safety car was deployed. Antonelli was called in, offered a cheap stop to move from hard tyres to mediums.

He came out flying, but 14 seconds behind race leader Russell, who had stayed out and was thus handed the uphill task of making his harder rubber last sufficiently well to the end with an ever-diminishing advantage.

At times, the to-be-winner Antonelli lapped nearly a second quicker than Russell and it grew into a matter of not if but when he would close the deficit to his senior before the 53rd and concluding lap.

Kimi Antonelli roared to victory in his home Grand Prix, becoming the first Italian to win it since 1966

It set up a grandstand finish. With 10 laps remaining, Antonelli was 4.7sec back. It looked bleak for Russell. It was going to come down to the last nervous moments. Or not quite as long as that, in fact.

Antonelli arrived on Russell’s gearbox on lap 49. They skirmished at the first corner. All fair. Russell went deep. Antonelli ran into the gravel, losing two seconds. Russell kept the lead, for now. But a lap later Antonelli did what the inevitable at Variante Ascari: he went into first place, and that was that.

His Mercedes was fast and Monza is an overtaking track, but this was also a scintillating drive, albeit helped by this strategy that was most useful to him.

An early red flag brought about by Charles Leclerc’s huge shunt on lap two got him on to hard tyres under the red-flag opportunity and bunched the field (a huge help after his engine change had condemned to start so far down the field).

Russell, arguably, should have been far enough up the road never to have been under threat. He had, after all, started 17 places ahead of Antonelli, who transported himself from further back on the grid to win than anyone since John Watson at Long Beach, California in 1983. Watson started 22nd that day.

The Mercedes garage hailed the win as you would expect – with unbridled emotion, and their motorhome was buzzing afterwards. Antonelli is their favoured son. Russell, who finished 3.8sec back from him, is not. He is also 66 points adrift from leader Antonelli in the standings and has precisely no momentum with 10 races remaining.

It is almost impossible to see a way back for Russell. He has won twice this season; Antonelli seven times.

George Russell, starting second and finishing second, could only congratulate his team-mate

But why did Mercedes not bring Russell, then leading, in for new tyres rather Antonelli? Their team boss Toto Wolff said: ‘We didn’t know what was the better strategy.

‘At that stage, the system said that the one-stop (Russell’s strategy) comes out ahead. That is what the software said.’

On whether Russell’s championship dream folded in the Royal Park at Monza, Wolff added: ‘It’s too early to say. It’s motor racing. It’s a technical sport. Things can break. Accidents can happen, and that’s why we have to do our best job for both drivers.’

If that sounds as if Wolff believes in and is backing Russell, I’m Mother Theresa. The Austrian said Antonelli is improving like an AI agent and that he had ‘walked on water’ here.

Russell was strangely sanguine afterwards, saying: ‘Kimi is definitely in charge of the championship, and he deserves to be. I am not even thinking about a fight or a comeback but focused on taking it race by race and maximising every weekend.

Early on the race was suspended following Charles Leclerc's 160mph smash into the barriers

‘It is going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap, so I am sort of accepting what it is. I am going to try to enjoy it from here and win as many races as possible.’

Max Verstappen, for the record, finished third. Lando Norris was fourth and Oscar Piastri fifth. Lewis Hamilton was sixth for Ferrari.

It was a yo-yoing race, a good show in some ways but one that revealed not only the strengths but the frailties of the new regulations introduced this year that allow one car to pass with a boost button and then be repassed as their electric charge falls off.

Early, Leclerc was left sitting in pain after his dramatic 160mph crash.

The Ferrari favourite lost control of his car at the final bend, the Parabolica, as he duelled with Piastri for fourth place.

Leclerc’s impact with the wall was severe with only a short portion of gravel to slow his trajectory into the hoardings, which he thudded side-on.

Leclerc was left devastated on the grass after crashing out of the race

The Monegasque soon jumped out of the car but then sat disconsolately on the grass as he was comforted by a marshal before being taken away in the medical car. He was feeling his neck as he went for treatment. Ferrari said he had been released from the medical feeling ‘OK’.

The race was red-flagged for 30 minutes and some fans in the grandstands cried at the huge blow for their team.

By this point, Leclerc had already squeezed Hamilton on the second part of the opening chicane and was driving somewhat erratically. Hamilton was furious, saying: ‘Charles pushed me off.’ The seven-time world champion, who started fourth, fell down to 10th place.

Russell was leading the race for Mercedes at this point when the race was suspended after passing pole man Pierre Gasly, who was to finish seventh for Alpine, on the main straight at the end of the first lap.

Leclerc’s stricken car was taken away by crane and the ding-donging began again. And nobody was hit harder than Russell.

Sports.title: Formidable Arsenal already look like they have too much for the rest - nobody can match their completeness as they beat Xabi Alonso's resurgent Chelsea to lay down an early marker, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
They are childhood friends from San Sebastian, who played football on Playa de la Concha, and received eclectic football educations that were influenced by the minds of men like Johan Cruyff, Pep Guardiola and Rafa Benitez.

They were both fine, cultured midfielders, thinkers who were born to be distinguished coaches. They met as coaches for the first time on Sunday, dressed identically in the style of the fashionable manager, short-sleeved shirts, dark slacks and pumps with dashes of white.

But they are not in Basque Country any more. English football has them now. And on Sunday afternoon, they were swallowed up by its passions and its glories. The managers of Arsenal and Chelsea masterminded an absolute barn-burner of a game, a contest full of sound and fury and, sometimes, footballing beauty that was a credit to both of them.

At the end of the breathlessness, Arsenal ran out 2-1 winners and even at this early stage of the season, it felt significant. Chelsea had come here as pretenders to Arsenal’s throne after a swashbuckling start to their campaign but even though they did themselves credit, they could not quite keep pace with the champions.

Xabi Alonso’s side still produced some stunning attacking football and broke with lightning speed and skill. This result suggested that they will improve dramatically on their 10th-place finish last season but that they still have to take another step forward to be a match for Arteta’s side.

This Chelsea has many attributes but it cannot quite match Arsenal’s completeness. Arsenal are an eight or nine out of 10 everywhere on the field. And their substitutes are on the same level. Chelsea have weaknesses in defence and midfield that were their undoing at the Emirates and will be again. They are, at least, on an upward trajectory again.

Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso embrace before their sides played out a pulsating 90 minutes

Martin Odegaard keeps his cool to fire Arsenal's winner early in the second half

But Arsenal look formidable. That is three wins from their first three league games now and even though they were pressed close at Villa Park last Monday and again by Chelsea, they have never looked like losing. And they have always looked like the better team. They just have too much for the rest. That is the way it looks now anyway.

It had taken Chelsea less than two minutes to take the lead. Reece James floated a free-kick into the Arsenal box and it bobbed around from head to head as the home side tried to clear it. Eventually, it fell to Morgan Rogers. Chelsea’s new £117m signing let the ball drop and then hit a controlled right-foot volley beyond the dive of David Raya. It was a precise shot but Raya would have been disappointed not to save it.

Two minutes later, Arsenal should have been level from a free-kick of their own. It was a clever routine. Martin Odegaard hit a low, skimmer of a ball to the near post where Riccardo Calafiori peeled away from his marker and got to it first. Any contact would have meant a goal but Calafiori missed it and Emiliano Martinez, a former Arsenal keeper, saved with his legs.

In the melee that followed, as the ball became stuck in a tangle of legs and prone bodies, Martinez was kicked in the head by Gabriel as they lay on the floor. Chelsea wanted a red card. Referee Chris Kavanagh demurred. Next, another melee. This time, Calafiori forced it over the line but VAR showed Ezri Konsa, making his home debut, had strayed offside.

It was a breathless opening. Martinez saved at close range from Bukayo Saka, Joao Pedro was booked for kneeing the ball away, Kai Havertz had a shot blocked by Wesley Fofana. Declan Rice went to take the resulting corner, to be greeted by ranks of Chelsea fans holding aloft inflatable replicas of the Champions League trophy, to remind Arsenal they have never won it.

The pace did not abate. Raya saved a piledriver from Joao Pedro, Havertz wasted an Arsenal breakaway with a failed flick meant for Odegaard, Joao Pedro flung himself at a slide-rule pass from Cole Palmer that eluded him by inches. And then, at the end of it all, Arsenal equalised.

Morgan Rogers clashes with his England team-mate Declan Rice during a fractious moment

The build-up was innocuous. The ball was fed to Havertz close to the right touchline. He darted inside and ran across the face of the box. He unleashed a left-foot shot that squeezed through the legs of Maxence Lacroix. Martinez got down to it and got his left hand to it but he could only push it into the corner of the net. He, too, would have been disappointed not to save it.

The half finished as it had begun. Pedro Neto raced away down the right as Arsenal’s defence desperately tried to keep pace with him. Neto cut inside on to his left foot and drilled in a shot from the edge of the area that beat the dive of Raya but cannoned off his right-hand post.

Arsenal took the lead five minutes after the break. Christos Tzolis played a low ball in from the right to Havertz. Havertz executed a sublime dummy that left Wesley Fofana rooted to the spot. The ball ran on to Odegaard, who took a touch and then lashed the ball high beyond Martinez.

Arsenal pushed for a third. Martinez saved well from a Saka curler, James headed off the line after Havertz had flicked on a near post corner and when a corner from Saka bounced off the boot of Havertz a yard from the line, it looped up in a shallow arc and landed in the hands of Martinez as he lay on the turf.

Kai Havertz levelled for the Gunners by squeezing a shot through Chelsea's defence

Rogers got Chelsea off to the perfect start with a goal in the second minute

Now it was Chelsea’s turn to press for an equaliser. James let fly from 25 yards out and it was a measure of this redoubtable Arsenal defence that Gabriel stood resolutely in the way of it a ball hurtling towards him like a bullet and headed it away.

Raya produced a brilliant save to tip over a curling effort from substitute Estevao that was destined for the top corner and Arsenal resorted to other means to keeping Chelsea at bay, too.

Six minutes from the end, Rogers burst forward to try to get on to a pass and was brought down by a cynical trip from behind by Declan Rice. Rogers reacted angrily and there was a brief fracas before the men were pulled apart.

‘You should have signed for a big club,’ the Arsenal fans chanted at Rogers, who had been courted by Arsenal before he chose to sign for their London rivals.

Chelsea are looking like a big club again at last but they may not quite be ready to challenge Arsenal’s supremacy in the league this season.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho already 'disinterested' as ex-Man Utd star sets alarm bells ringing
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho already 'disinterested' as ex-Man Utd star sets alarm bells ringing

Alejandro Garnacho has been torn apart by former Liverpool left-back Stephen Warnock after struggling during Aston Villa's goalless draw at Hull City

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho in action for Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United and Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho has been told he looked "completely disinterested" on his third appearance for Aston Villa.

The 22-year-old, who joined the Villans on loan with a conditional obligation to buy from Chelsea earlier this summer, came on as a second-half substitute during his side's 0-0 draw against Hull City on Saturday. The Argentine came on for Emiliano Buendia in the 75th minute as Unai Emery's men searched for their first win of the season.

But Garnacho struggled when he was introduced and failed to make an impact. Indeed, he didn't have a single shot, create a chance, complete a cross and made just nine passes during 15 minutes plus stoppage-time.

With Garnacho having a difficult cameo, ex-Villa and Liverpool left-back Stephen Warnock tore into the winger for his performance and believes he - and Tammy Abraham - did nothing when they came on the pitch. Abraham was brought on in the 85th minute by Emery with Nicolas Jackson coming off.

Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low READ MORE :

Michael Carrick points finger at Man Utd stars after late Everton draw READ MORE :

Speaking on co-commentary, Warnock said: "You may as well take off Alejandro Garnacho and Tammy Abraham. They have done nothing since they have come on the pitch. Garnacho going down. He looks completely disinterested. Unai Emery will be furious with his changes."

Garnacho exited United last summer after making 144 first-team appearances for the Reds, scoring 26 goals. He moved to Chelsea for £40million, though he endured a miserable debut season in west London.

This prompted the Blues to sanction his exit, with Villa snapping him up in July. Since then, Garnacho has appeared in Villa's opening three Premier League fixtures this term, but has been kept of the side by teenager George Hemmings, who has been a standout performer for the Villans.

View 2 Images Garnacho has yet to start for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

When asked about how Hemmings has cemented that position, Emery admitted after the Hull match that Hemmings is already operating at Premier League standard, while Garnacho still requires development.

"George, he worked last year the whole year with us and played minutes," Emery said. "He is performing fantastic and getting better. He created one assist for Buendia. He is working in the intensity and kilometres we need. He is doing it. I think he is a player now, clearly, to be in the Premier League.

"Then, we have other players who joined who need to adapt to us in training, playing matches, and Garnacho is in this way. We need their performance to try to add things, working and getting numbers. Garnacho is in this way. How he is responding, George, is really fantastic."

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool and Newcastle ace vindicated after wife refused to move for transfer
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool and Newcastle ace vindicated after wife refused to move for transfer

Former Liverpool goalkeeper Loris Karius decided to move to German side Schalke after his exit from Newcastle United despite the wishes of his wife Diletta Leotta

View 3 Images Loris Karius has enjoyed a crowning moment following his suprising move to Schalke in 2025 (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool and Newcastle goalkeeper Loris Karius put in a man of the match peformance as Schalke pulled off a remarkable draw against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga. The German side were promoted to the top-flight but lost their opening match against Augsburg before producing a stunning upset against the champions.

‌



Karius kept a clean sheet in the goalless draw and earned plaudits from his opposite number, Manuel Neuer, in a jubilant moment for Die Knappen. The 33-year-old was central to ending two Bayern records as the stalemate marked the first time in 59 competitive matches that Bayern failed to score and the first time in 67 Bundesliga matchdays that Bayern will not finish the weekend at the top of the table.

‌



"Loris Karius was very good and definitely the right choice for Man of the Match. We had three big chances that he kept out," Neuer admitted. "That was definitely key to us not winning this game."

‌



Karius was happy to credit his team-mates for their efforts, suggesting that he didn't have much to do despite his notable impact. "It was great for me," he said.

Gary Neville issues on-air apology as VAR statement released on Arsenal goal vs Chelsea READ MORE :

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite failed coup and calls to leave READ MORE :

"I only had to shout to keep going, move up, drop back. Real credit to the guys for what they did.

"They kept so much away and made things so incredibly hard for Bayern.

‌



"The guys really worked hard until they couldn't go anymore. Everyone today can be proud of their performance."

View 3 Images Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany congratulates Loris Karius (Image: UWE KRAFT / AFP via Getty Images)

Karius joined Schalke as a free agent 18 months ago, joining the side as back up to Justin Heekeren. The German goalkeeper, who started his senior career with Mainz, joined the club in January 2025 in controversial circumstances.

‌



Having gone without a club following the expiry of his contract at Newcastle, Karius opted to move to Germany against the wishes of his life Diletta Leotta. The television presenter had hoped that her husband would join her in Italy where she has been a part of Serie A broadcasting.

Leotta was said to have struggled to understand Karius' move to Germany as he attempts to kickstart his career once again. His efforts against Bayern might have been some vindication.

View 3 Images Diletta Leotta and her husband Loris Karius walk the carpet at the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup Draw (Image: Leonardo Fernandez - FIFA)

‌



Speaking following his move in 2025, Karius admitted that Leotta was full behind it regardless of her feelings. "Of course she was hoping a little for Italy," Karius told reporters.

"I explained it to her. She wishes me the best in my career and said she is fully behind it.

"Milan is not far away. We can find ways to solve it. She has a lot to do too, so we will both be commuting back and forth a bit.

Article continues below

"If your partner is also in the public eye, it's clear that something will be reported. But I never actively pushed myself into it. For me, the sport was always the priority."

Sports.title: Maitland-Niles screamer breaks Man Utd hearts and earns Everton draw - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Maitland-Niles screamer breaks Man Utd hearts and earns Everton draw - 5 talking points

EVERTON 2-2 MAN UTD: The Red Devils looked set to be on the way to three huge points at Hill Dickinson Stadium only for debutant Ainsley Maitland-Niles to secure a share of the spoils

View 3 Images Ainsley Maitland-Niles enjoyed a dream debut for Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored an absolute stunner to steal a point against Manchester United on his Everton debut.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo struck the opener moments into the second half following a barnstorming run and lethal finish. Tyrique George thought he had ensured a share of the points, only for Benjamin Sesko to nod home late on to seemingly steal victory.

‌



The drama was not over there as Maitland-Niles climbws off the bench to fire home a late cracker to seal a draw for Everton and David Moyes.

‌



Here are all of the talking points from Hill Dickinson Stadium:

Chances wasted

After his treble against Ipswich last weekend, Bruno Fernandes unsurprisingly went the closest to opening the scoring on Merseyside, having struck the bar with a powerful volley. Matheus Cunha then had a great opportunity but blazed over.

‌



Thierno Barry should have given the home side the lead before the break as he got on the end of a teasing cross but lifted his header over. While chances came and went, fans did not have to wait long for the goals to come.

Mbeumo blasts Man Utd ahead

While United were left frustrated in the first half, it didn't take long into the second for Michael Carrick's men to hit the front. After picking up the ball on the right flank, he cut inside and charged past a number of challenges before firing a lethal drive into the bottom corner.

It represented his second goal of the season, as well as his first-ever career goal against Everton.

‌



View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo celebrates his second goal of the season (Image: Getty Images)

George answers Moyes call

There is one sure-fire way to get the crowd back on side and that's a stunning goal. And that's exactly what George provided.

The former Chelsea youngster received the ball on the right and thumped a brilliant effort into the roof of the net. Having been beaten at his near post, Senne Lammens might have felt he could have done better.

‌



But George will not care one jot. The forward has been backed to become an emergency striker by boss Moyes and given his finish, he might not be far wrong.

Sesko the super sub

Coming into this season, there was hope that Benjamin Sesko would begin to stamp his authority over the side. That has not quite come to fruition quite yet.

Ahead of the trip to Merseyside, Sesko had yet to find the net this season. But he was in the right place at the right time to nod home for the Red Devils.

‌



And while he might have a feeling of disappointment right now that his goal was not the winner, it might just be the tonic he needs to ignite his season and, hopefully, his Manchester United career.

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko thought he was the matchwinner at Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Maitland-Niles announces himself

The arrival of Ainsley Maitland-Niles might not have been the inspirational signing that Everton fans wanted on deadline day despite the dire need for a right-back. Some might suggest that they're feeling a little bit silly now.

Article continues below

The former Arsenal man fired home an absolutely stunning effort deep into stoppage time to seal a point. And that might just be what Everton and boss Moyes need to lift the gloom on Merseyside.

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Ian Wright disagree over six Premier League stars - 'Not having that'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville and Ian Wright disagree over six Premier League stars - 'Not having that'

Arsenal face Chelsea in Saturday's Premier League blockbuster at the Emirates Stadium as both teams look to protect their perfect starts to the season

View 2 Images Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville and Ian Wright got into a disagreement about the quality of the forward lines in the Arsenal and Chelsea squads. The sides go head-to-head in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon, where both the Gunners and the Blues have a 100 percent record on the line.

‌



Arsenal defeated Coventry City and Aston Villa in their first two Premier League matches of the season, while Chelsea earned wins over Fulham and Brighton.

‌



Wright and Neville were part of Sky Sports’ punditry team for their coverage of Arsenal vs Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium, and the duo got into a debate about the forward options available to Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta.

‌



Neville suggested that he believes Arteta would prefer Chelsea's attacking resources over the players currently at his disposal at Arsenal.

Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea star's position switch before Arsenal showdown READ MORE :

"If you say to Mikel Arteta: 'Would you swap your forward line for Chelsea's?' He would swap," Neville said.

"He'd put [Morgan] Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro up there in front of [Bukayo] Saka, [Kai] Havertz and [Ebere] Eze, he would. So it's not the strongest part of Arsenal's team, but what he's done in defence and in midfield has become that good.

‌



"If you don't concede goals, you've got a great chance of winning nearly every single match. If you're conceding goals, you're going to lose more points."

Wright, however, took exception to Neville's view, with the Arsenal icon responding: "I'm not having that over Saka, Havertz and Eze. I'm not having that."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal and Chelsea go head-to-head on Sunday afternoon

Neville then responded by saying: "You don't think he'd [Arteta] pick Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro over those three [Havertz, Saka and Eze], Ian?"

Wright replied: "Not for me, no." Neville then concluded the debate by saying: "Oh dear."

‌



Arsenal strengthened their attacking options this summer by bringing in Christos Tzolis, though they sanctioned the exits of Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus.

Chelsea, meanwhile, have also strengthened their forward line considerably, with Rogers being joined by Geovany Quenda, Danny Welbeck, Emmanuel Emegha and Dastan Satpaev in making the move to Stamford Bridge before week's deadline.

Sports.title: F1 Italian GP suspended after huge Charles Leclerc crash and Lewis Hamilton battle
Sports.content:
F1 Italian GP suspended after huge Charles Leclerc crash and Lewis Hamilton battle

The Italian Grand Prix was brought to a halt after Charles Leclerc crashed into the tyre wall at Monza

View 2 Images Charles Leclerc crashed into the tyre wall on the second lap of the Italian Grand Prix. (Image: Sky Sports)

The Italian Grand Prix was red-flagged just two laps into the iconic Monza race after Charles Leclerc suffered a major crash. The Monegasque driver collided with the tyre wall on the second lap after losing control of his Ferrari at the tail end of the Parabolica.

‌



The 28-year-old was able to exit the car and appeared to be winded as he walked away from the wreckage. The rear end of the Ferrari got away from Leclerc as he attempted to correct the slide, but he couldn't keep the car on the track, skidding off the gravel and hitting the wall at some speed - with a force later revealed to be at 60G.

‌



The race was brought to a halt soon after, with red flags out on track, to allow the safety team to recover Leclerc's car from the gravel trap and make repairs to the tyre wall.

‌



Lewis Hamilton risks Charles Leclerc wrath with request to Ferrari bosses READ MORE :

F1 star stripped of podium 48 hours before Italian GP in double penalty as FIA announce ruling READ MORE :

It was an awful start for Ferrari in their home Grand Prix with both of the Prancing Horse drivers battling it out in the early stages of the race.

Lewis Hamilton dropped to P10 and claimed he was pushed off the track by Leclerc on the team radio, with his title hopes drifting away. The incident was noted by the FIA, but it's unlikely anything will come of it, given Leclerc's crash.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Hamilton is expected to restart the race in P8 after regaining some positions, but Ferrari were dealt a huge blow when Leclerc crashed, having been battling for P2 against Pierre Gasly.

The Alpine driver started the race in a shock first pole position of his career, but Gasly was caught by George Russell's Mercedes down the straight at the end of the first lap.

View 2 Images Charles Leclerc suffered a major crash at the Italian Grand Prix

‌



Championship leader Kimi Antonelli began from the rear of the grid following an engine penalty, but the teenage sensation had worked his way up to P12.

The restart came from a standing start with Russell on pole and Gasly alongside him on the second row. Franco Colapinto moved up to P4 after getting past Piastri in the wake of Leclerc's crash, but before the red flag was deployed.

It's been a disappointing couple of weeks for the Ferrari duo, with Hamilton frustrated that Leclerc didn't let him pass in their last race outing at Zandvoort, despite being the faster of the two cars.

Article continues below

Leclerc's crash means that Ferrari need a strong end to the race from Hamilton with only one of their cars left out on the track.

Sports.title: Police launch investigation after Cardiff City star appeared to grab young fan by the neck
Sports.content:
Police launch investigation after Cardiff City star appeared to grab young fan by the neck

Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik clashed with a young Portsmouth supporter during the Bluebirds' 2-0 defeat at Fratton Park on Saturday afternoon

View 2 Images Krystian Bielik clashed with a Portsmouth fan

Hampshire Police have launched an investigation into an alleged common assault after a Cardiff City player appeared to grab a young Portsmouth supporter by the neck during a clash on Saturday.

Portsmouth's 2-0 win over the Bluebirds was overshadowed by unsavoury scenes in the 70th minute of the Championship match. Krystian Bielik went over to the sidelines to collect the ball in order to take a throw-in, only to become involved in a heated exchange with a nearby fan.

Replays appeared to show the 28-year-old former Arsenal star grabbing the youngster by the throat. Bielik was then slapped by the fan, who was led out of the stadium by stewards along with his family. The match was briefly stopped by the referee in order to cool the situation down.

Hampshire Police are now investigating the incident, which will also be the subject of a Football Association investigation after being included in the referee's report.

A Hampshire Police spokesperson told Mirror Football: "We can confirm that we are investigating an incident in which a teenage boy was reportedly the victim of a common assault during yesterday’s (Saturday 5 September) football match at Fratton Park. Our enquiries are ongoing."

Article continues below

Portsmouth said in a statement: “Portsmouth Football Club are aware of supporter concerns regarding the incident involving a young fan and an opposition player at yesterday’s match at Fratton Park.

“As this remains a safeguarding matter and is currently under investigation by both the club and the police, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further on the circumstances at this time. However, we are aware that a number of claims and assertions are circulating on social media. We would urge caution against speculation while enquiries are ongoing.

“The welfare and safeguarding of young people are of paramount importance to Portsmouth Football Club. We will continue to liaise with the relevant parties as enquiries progress. No further comment will be made at this stage while investigations remain ongoing.”

A Cardiff City spokesperson said: "Cardiff City FC is aware of a confrontation between a small section of Portsmouth supporters and Krystian Bielik at Fratton Park yesterday.

View 2 Images Krystian Bielik joined Cardiff this summer (Image: Adam Fradgley/Getty Images)

"We are satisfied with the way that match officials dealt with the situation during the game, having been in full view of it. Player protection will always be of paramount importance to us.

"It is understood that due process will be undertaken following the submission of the referee’s report to the Football Association. As such it would not be appropriate to comment further on the matter at this time.”

Speaking after the game, Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy said: "I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is. I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably. I was assured by him the correct processes will take place.

"He said he’d seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

Article continues below

"The players are always subjected to different things that’s not acceptable. My job is to protect the players, but really I’m trying to make sure that we play well and win. I’m sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes."

Sports.title: Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low
Sports.content:
Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low

Alejandro Garnacho has endured a very difficult few seasons and his loan spell with Aston Villa appears to have got off to a tricky start following his switch from Chelsea

View 2 Images Garnacho is set to spend the season on loan with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery believes Alejandro Garnacho still needs time to adapt having played just half an hour for the club. The Argentine forward joined Villa on loan this summer from Chelsea.

‌



There is an obligation to make that move permanent at the end of this season should certain conditions be met. But Garnacho’s contributions in the Midlands have been limited so far.

‌



He has made just three substitute appearances for Villa so far this season, while he has also fallen behind academy graduate George Hemmings in the pecking order. Asked how he has managed to earn that position, Emery has suggested that the youngster is already a Premier League player, while Garnacho still has work to do.

‌



Speaking after his side’s 0-0 draw with Hull City on Saturday, Emery said: “George, he worked last year the whole year with us and played minutes. He is performing fantastic and getting better.

“He created one assist for Buendia. He is working in the intensity and kilometres we need. He is doing it. I think he is a player now, clearly, to be in the Premier League.

‌



“Then, we have other players who joined who need to adapt to us in training, playing matches, and Garnacho is in this way.

“We need their performance to try to add things, working and getting numbers. Garnacho is in this way. How he is responding, George, is really fantastic.”

Garnacho’s move to Villa follows a very tricky couple of years for him. He fell out of favour at Manchester United, ahead of a switch to Chelsea.

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho has yet to start for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

But he lasted just a year at Stamford Bridge, scoring just once in 24 Premier League appearances. He underlined his desire to rediscover his confidence during his time with Aston Villa.

"This is an important club which is going up really quickly, so I can't wait to get started here," Garnacho said after his switch to Villa was announced. "I was looking for a club to get my confidence back, so I can try to become the player I was a few years ago in my first years at Manchester United.

Article continues below

"I spoke with the manager and he gave me the confidence to try to help the team here - that's why I'm here. It is important to play in European competitions and the Champions League is the best one, so the fact we are playing in it this season makes me really happy. Hopefully we can do something important in it."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
