World.title: Hungary to open third heavy-freight route to Serbia as border crossing gets major upgrade
World.content:
Hungary is preparing a major new freight corridor towards Serbia, with the Hercegszántó–Bački Breg border crossing set for a full reconstruction that would allow heavy lorries to cross around the clock.

The Hungarian government has approved the full reconstruction of the Hercegszántó–Bački Breg border crossing, aimed at easing chronic congestion at Röszke and creating a new route linking Serbia with southern Hungary and the M6 motorway, Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy announced on Sunday.

According to the minister, the Transport and Investment Ministry is expected to launch the public procurement procedure for construction in the coming weeks.

The project would significantly expand the role of Hercegszántó in cross-border traffic. At present, international heavy goods vehicles can cross the Hungarian–Serbian border only at Röszke and Tompa, while Röszke regularly struggles with several-kilometre queues. Vitézy said as many as 30,000–40,000 vehicles a day pass through Röszke during peak periods.

Heavy lorries to get a new route between Hungary and Serbia

Once the reconstruction is completed, Hercegszántó will also be able to handle heavy goods vehicles. Plans include separate lanes for lorries and buses, greater capacity for passenger cars, a parking area for around 40–42 trucks, and facilities for pedestrians and cyclists. Heavy freight traffic would be accommodated on a continuous, 24-hour basis.

There is an important distinction for travellers: Hercegszántó–Bački Breg is not a completely new border crossing. Hungary’s tax and customs authority currently lists it as operating 24 hours a day for international passenger traffic and freight vehicles with a maximum permissible weight of 3.5 tonnes.

The reconstruction will therefore primarily transform the existing crossing into a major heavy-freight route.

Vitézy said the development had already been approved years ago by the previous government, but construction did not proceed because funding was not provided. Plans and the necessary permits are already available, according to the minister.

If you missed it: Hungary fuel prices face first major test as oil climbs and government rules out costly cap

New corridor could take pressure off Röszke and the M5

According to Vitézy, the upgraded crossing could eventually create a new transport corridor linking Vojvodina with southern Hungary and the M6 motorway via the new Mohács bridge. In the longer term, the route could take some traffic away from Röszke, as well as from the heavily used M5 motorway and the southern section of Budapest’s M0 ring road.

Development is also taking place on the Serbian side of the border. Serbia is working on the “Smile of Vojvodina” expressway, with the first 22.8-kilometre section planned between Bački Breg and Sombor. The section is expected to be completed within roughly two years, although the wider expressway project will take considerably longer.

Horgos/Röszke. Photo: MTI

The combination of the Serbian expressway, the upgraded border crossing and improved connections towards the M6 could eventually provide an alternative north–south route for freight travelling between the Balkans and Hungary.

Government scales back part of connecting road project

The border upgrade also forms part of a wider debate over road development around Mohács.

Vitézy said that even with the new Serbian connection, traffic forecasts do not justify building the entire corridor as a 2×2-lane road. He pointed out that Serbia is not a member of the European Union and would likely remain outside the Schengen Area for some time even after eventual EU accession, meaning border controls themselves would continue to limit traffic capacity.

The government therefore plans to redesign parts of the route between Main Road 51 and Mohács as a 2×1-lane road, with the money saved redirected towards other transport investments, road renovations and the border crossing itself.

World.title: Korean Film Festival returns to Budapest with 24 films, demon hunters and a zombie comedy
World.content:
Korean cinema returns to Budapest this September with 24 feature films, three visiting directors and a programme stretching from historical drama to occult action and zombie comedy.

The 19th Korean Film Festival will run from 25 September to 2 October at Budapest’s Corvin Cinema, offering audiences a broader look at South Korean filmmaking beyond global hits such as Parasite and Squid Game.

Organised by the Korean Cultural Center, this year’s festival is divided into four sections – Fresh, Faces, Focus and Extra – and will also feature post-screening conversations with three Korean directors.

From a child king to demon hunters

The festival opens with Chang Hang-jun’s historical drama The King’s Warden, set in 15th-century Joseon. The story follows the leader of an impoverished mountain village who is unexpectedly entrusted with Yi Hong-wi, a young king forced from the throne.

Elsewhere, the programme moves rapidly between genres. Heartman: Rock and Love brings a former musician face to face with his first love, while The Ugly begins with human remains discovered after four decades.

At the more spectacular end of the line is Holy Night: Demon Hunters, in which three people with supernatural abilities attempt to save Seoul from a devil-worshipping criminal organisation.

A scene from Holy Night: Demon Hunters, one of the festival’s supernatural action highlights. Photo: Korean Cultural Center

An 80-day journey from Gwangju to Budapest

One film has an unusually direct Hungarian connection.

3 Gen. Journey follows a grandfather, a father and two children travelling by electric car from Gwangju to Budapest over 80 days. It forms part of the festival’s Focus: On the Road selection, built around journeys that do not always end where their protagonists expect.

Three generations set out on an 80-day electric-car journey from Gwangju to Budapest in 3 Gen. Journey. Photo: Korean Cultural Center

Budapest audiences will also have the opportunity to meet Korean filmmakers in person. Song Jinuk and Jang Kunjae will take part in CineTalk events on 26 September, followed by Lee Seonyeon on 27 September. The discussions will be held in Hungarian and Korean.

A scene from Journey to Gyeongju, part of the festival’s “On the Road” selection. Photo: Korean Cultural Center

Korean independent cinema gets its own spotlight

The festival’s Extra section will present five films selected with its official partner, the Jeonju International Film Festival.

The line-up explores relationships, financial insecurity, family ties and historical trauma. Among the more unusual titles is documentary Horoomon, which uses the history of a popular Japanese dish to explore the identity and exclusion experienced by the Korean minority in Japan.

Zombie comedy closes the Festival

The festival closes on 2 October with comedy My Daughter is a Zombie. Adapted from a popular webtoon, it follows a father who refuses to abandon his daughter after she becomes a zombie. He hides her in the countryside with her grandmother and attempts to teach her how to behave like a human again.

A scene from My Daughter is a Zombie, the closing film of the 19th Korean Film Festival in Budapest. Photo: Korean Cultural Center

Despite the supernatural premise, the film is ultimately built around the relationship between father and daughter.

The Festival will take place at Corvin Cinema in Budapest from 25 September to 2 October 2026.

Venue: Corvin Cinema, 1082 Budapest, Corvin köz 1.

Tickets: available from 10 September, both online via Corvin Cinema and at the cinema box office

Programme and further information: koreaifilmfesztival.hu

Facebook event: available on the festival’s official event page

World.title: Budapest Half Marathon breaks participation record with runners from 117 countries
World.content:
Budapest saw a new participation record at the 41st Wizz Air Budapest Half Marathon on Sunday, with more than 24,000 entries.

More than 24,000 people registered for the event, surpassing last year’s previous record. The field included runners from 117 countries, while Hungarian participants arrived from around 1,200 towns and villages across the country.

The scale of the event was clear from the very beginning. Competitors set off from Pázmány Péter Promenade, but with such a large field, the staggered starting process itself lasted almost 50 minutes.

Alongside the traditional 21.1-kilometre half marathon, runners could also take part in a 10-kilometre race, giving the event a broader mass-participation character.

Hungarian champions defend their titles

The event also hosted the Hungarian Half Marathon Championships, where both defending champions retained their titles.

In the men’s race, Gábor Karsai successfully defended his national title in 1:04:19. Máté Dávid Vásárhelyi finished second in 1:07:27, while Ákos Molnár took third in 1:07:31.

Lili Anna Vindics-Tóth was even more dominant in the women’s event, retaining her title with a major personal best of 1:09:21. Viktória Niesz finished second in 1:18:46, with Nóra Nagy third in 1:19:36.

Both the half-marathon and 10-kilometre races reached their maximum entry limits before race day. The starting straight alone stretched for around 600 metres, helping organisers manage what they described as the largest half-marathon start ever staged in Hungary.

Another upcoming sport event: Budapest is about to host an athletics event unlike any before – $10 million in prize money and no medals

Foreign running tourism surges in Budapest

One of the clearest trends behind this year’s record is the rapid growth of international running tourism. According to the Budapest Sport Office, 8,449 entries came from abroad, including 7,330 foreign runners in the half marathon itself.

Organisers say international participation has increased by around 300% compared with the pre-Covid period, turning the Budapest Half Marathon into an increasingly important event on the European autumn running calendar.

The growth is particularly striking compared with last year. In 2025, just over 6,300 international runners entered the race, and organisers estimated that foreign participants generated around 40,000 guest nights in Budapest. This year’s overseas field is substantially larger again, although no comparable tourism figure has yet been published for 2026.

Two tonnes of medals for a sold-out race

The scale of the event could also be seen in the preparations. Organisers had to produce around two tonnes of finisher medals for the 2026 race. Their design features the outline of Budapest and the River Danube, while the course itself takes runners through several of the capital’s World Heritage areas.

World.title: Body of missing 21-year-old Ozora Festival crew member found near festival site
World.content:
More than a month after he disappeared, 21-year-old OZORA Festival crew member Bence Szolnoki has been found dead near the festival grounds.

The festival said the Fejér County Police Headquarters had officially confirmed that Szolnoki’s body was found on Friday outside the festival area. Szolnoki was a member of Ozora’s on-site crew and had been involved in preparing the festival before his disappearance.

“It is with great sadness that we share with the O.Z.O.R.A. community that the body of Bence Szolnoki was found on Friday in a cornfield near the festival grounds,” the organisers said on its official Facebook page.

The festival described Szolnoki as both a colleague and a member of its community, noting that crew members live and work together throughout the months-long preparation period.

“We have lost a colleague and a member of our community,” the organisers said, extending their condolences to his family and loved ones.

Missing since late July

Hungarian police had been searching for Szolnoki since early August. According to an earlier police notice, the 21-year-old from Tahitótfalu travelled to a festival in Tolna County on 24 July for work and was last contacted by a family member on 26 July. Other reports based on information from his relatives said he was last seen at the O.Z.O.R.A. Festival in late July.

His disappearance prompted an extensive search involving police, volunteers and civil search teams, with parts of the area around the festival repeatedly searched in the weeks that followed. The organisers expressed their condolences to Szolnoki’s family and loved ones, saying his death was particularly painful because of his close connection to the festival team.

No official information has yet been released about the cause or circumstances of his death, and the discovery was first announced publicly by the festival on Sunday.

If you missed it: Hungarian police seize thousands of documents in investigation into state Eximbank deals

Third death connected to this year’s Ozora

Szolnoki’s death is the third linked to this year’s O.Z.O.R.A. Festival, although the circumstances of the three cases are different and there is no known connection between them.

Earlier in August, a 45-year-old American man died after climbing onto decorative structures near the main stage and falling. Police ruled out the involvement of a third party.

A 39-year-old woman also died during the festival after suffering sudden cardiac arrest. Emergency crews attempted to resuscitate her but were unable to save her life. Following those two deaths, organisers shortened the festival’s Sunday music programme.

Tragedy: Two festivalgoers die at Ozora Festival in Hungary

Cover image: Photo: Ozora Festival official / Facebook

World.title: Budapest is about to host an athletics event unlike any before – $10 million in prize money and no medals
World.content:
Budapest is preparing to host the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship, a brand-new global competition that will bring some of the world’s leading athletes to the Hungarian capital from 11 to 13 September.

The three-day event at the National Athletics Centre will break with the traditional World Championships format. With a record USD 10 million prize pot and some of the sport’s biggest names competing, organisers are promising a faster, higher-stakes spectacle.

Organisers have promised a compact, high-stakes format in which almost every session is packed with semi-finals and finals – and even the traditional medal ceremony has been reimagined.

World Athletics says the field will bring together Paris 2024 Olympic champions, Tokyo 2025 world champions, this year’s Diamond League winners and leading athletes from the world rankings.

The richest prize pot in athletics history

A total of USD 10 million will be distributed among the athletes, making it the largest prize fund ever offered at a single track and field event.

Winners of individual events will receive USD 150,000, while second-place finishers will earn USD 75,000 and third-place athletes USD 40,000. The winning teams in the relay events will share USD 80,000.

The competition will feature 26 individual events – 13 for men and 13 for women – as well as two mixed relay events.

Budapest’s National Athletics Centre, venue of the 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship. Photo: Facebook / World Athletics Ultimate Championship

Olympic champions from Paris 2024, world champions crowned in Tokyo in 2025 and this season’s Diamond League winners are among those eligible to compete. Athletes can also qualify through their world ranking, while a limited number may receive special invitations.

No gold, silver or bronze medals

One of the most unusual features of the new championship is that there will be no traditional gold, silver and bronze medals. Instead, World Athletics has designed a special trophy for each Ultimate Champion. Every participating athlete will receive a unique bracelet, which forms part of the winner’s trophy.

The specially designed trophy. Photo: Facebook / World Athletics Ultimate Championship

World Athletics President Sebastian Coe said the decision was intended to emphasise the championship’s central idea: identifying the single best athlete in each event rather than focusing on the traditional podium.

Read also: K-pop in Hungary is no longer just a teenage trend: it is becoming a cultural movement – interview

What to expect in Budapest

The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship will take place at the National Athletics Centre from 11 to 13 September, with three compact evening sessions built around semifinals and finals rather than long qualification rounds.

Spectators can expect a much faster-paced format than at a traditional world championship:

Friday, 11 September: men’s hammer, men’s pole vault, hurdles and mixed 4x100m relay

men’s hammer, men’s pole vault, hurdles and mixed 4x100m relay Saturday, 12 September: the big sprint night, with both the women’s and men’s 100m

the big sprint night, with both the women’s and men’s 100m Sunday, 13 September: 200m finals, middle-distance races and the mixed 4x400m relay

Hungarian fans will also have plenty to follow. Bence Halász is among the biggest home hopes in the hammer throw, while Boglárka Takács, Luca Kozák, Attila Molnár, Patrik Enyingi and Sára Mátó are also set to compete, alongside Hungarian teams in the mixed relays.

Tickets and venue

The championship will be held at the National Athletics Centre in Budapest, the same stadium that hosted the 2023 World Athletics Championships.

Tickets are available through the official World Athletics Ultimate Championship website, where spectators can also check current prices and seating options.

Key information:

Dates: 11–13 September 2026

11–13 September 2026 Venue: National Athletics Centre, Budapest

National Athletics Centre, Budapest Format: three evening sessions, focused on semifinals and finals

For Budapest, the event will mark another major international athletics weekend after the 2023 World Championships — this time in a shorter, faster format.

World.title: Chemical castration for child sex offenders? Controversial bill reaches Hungarian Parliament
World.content:
A Hungarian opposition MP has submitted a bill that would introduce so-called chemical castration for certain sex offenders in an effort to reduce the risk of repeat crimes against children. The proposal follows the Polish model, but the previous Orbán government rejected a similar idea on human rights and health grounds.

Előd Novák, an MP for the opposition Mi Hazánk party, submitted the proposal to the Hungarian National Assembly this week.

According to the bill, offenders considered at risk of committing further sexual crimes could undergo drug treatment aimed at reducing sexual drive, rather than relying primarily on psychiatric treatment in a closed institution.

Novák argues that Hungary’s existing rules do not sufficiently prevent repeat offending among this group and that stronger measures are needed to protect children. The treatment would be administered under the supervision of Hungary’s Judicial Observation and Psychiatric Institute (IMEI), with the drug-based form generally provided as outpatient care.

What does ‘chemical castration’ actually mean?

Despite the name, the proposal does not involve surgery. “Chemical castration” is a commonly used term for hormonal drug treatment, usually involving anti-androgen medication that suppresses the effects of male sex hormones and lowers testosterone levels.

Its purpose is to reduce sexual drive and, in theory, lower the risk of further sexual offending. As Index notes, medical professionals often prefer terms such as hormonal treatment or libido-reducing medication, as “chemical castration” can give a misleading impression of what the procedure involves.

The Mi Hazánk proposal explicitly points to Poland as a model.

Czechia has an even more controversial system. Pharmacological treatment is used there, while Czech law also continues to permit surgical castration in tightly regulated cases following a written request from the patient.

The Council of Europe’s anti-torture committee has repeatedly called for the practice to be abolished; its latest report said five applications for surgical castration were approved between 2018 and 2023.

If you missed it: Hungary fuel prices face first major test as oil climbs and government rules out costly cap

The idea has surfaced in Hungary before

The proposal is not entirely new to Hungarian politics. Dóra Dúró, now also a Mi Hazánk politician, raised similar proposals while she was a Jobbik MP, while other politicians on the nationalist right have called for stronger medical measures against child sex offenders over the years.

The issue returned to the political agenda after Hungary’s 2024 presidential pardon scandal, when Mi Hazánk leader László Toroczkai said his party would introduce castration for paedophile offenders if it came to power.

Orbán government previously rejected the measure

The previous Orbán government had already considered — and rejected — the idea. In 2013, Hungary’s Justice Ministry said the government did not plan to introduce chemical castration, pointing to constitutional and human rights protections concerning human dignity, physical and mental health, and the prohibition of torture or degrading treatment.

The ministry also warned at the time that the treatment could have serious health consequences and that its effectiveness in preventing further offences was not guaranteed.

For now, Novák’s proposal remains only a bill before parliament, with its prospects uncertain. Much will depend on whether Fidesz sticks to its earlier opposition and whether the governing Tisza majority is prepared to support the measure.

Here comes the twist: could Fidesz and Mi Hazánk be heading for a merger?

World.title: Trump peace mission draws rare positive response from Moscow after limited ceasefire
World.content:
Donald Trump’s latest effort to end Russia’s war in Ukraine is moving from Moscow to Kyiv after his top envoys spent three hours behind closed doors with Vladimir Putin. The Kremlin called the meeting constructive and signalled room for further talks, but Moscow also repeated several of its central demands.

Steve Witkoff, Trump’s special envoy, and Jared Kushner, the US president’s son-in-law and adviser, met Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday as Washington renewed its attempt to broker an end to the war.

Trump had said beforehand that the pair were carrying “a proposal to end the war”, while footage released by the Kremlin showed Putin acknowledging at the start of the meeting that the situation was “not so easy”. The talks lasted around three hours before the American delegation left Moscow for Kyiv, where Witkoff and Kushner are due to meet the Ukrainian leadership on Sunday.

A noticeably warmer tone from Moscow

The most striking feature of the meeting was the tone that followed it. Putin’s foreign policy adviser, Yury Ushakov, described the discussions as “substantive, very frank and constructive” and said several ideas for a possible peace settlement had been discussed.

Putin himself said direct contacts with the Americans were useful and spoke of a high level of trust in the negotiating relationship, according to BBC.

Witkoff also thanked Putin for the temporary restraint on strikes against Kyiv during the US visit, while the Russian president thanked Trump for his peace efforts.

The discussions were not limited to Ukraine. Ushakov said economic cooperation and potential large-scale Russian-American projects were also discussed, suggesting that both sides are looking beyond the immediate battlefield to the wider relationship between Moscow and Washington.

Read also: Hungary’s housing market faces a major shift as government backs social housing

But the hardest disagreements remain

The warmer rhetoric does not amount to a breakthrough. Ushakov said Putin again stressed what Moscow calls the “root causes” of the conflict and argued that Russia remained confident it could achieve its military objectives.

Russia still occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory, while Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart over territory, security guarantees and Ukraine’s future relationship with NATO.

The BBC noted that despite Russia’s repeated claims of battlefield momentum, its ground forces have generally advanced slowly and at enormous cost.

Al Jazeera also reported a somewhat less pessimistic mood around this round of diplomacy, partly because the Kremlin believes Russia currently holds the military advantage. At the same time, its Moscow correspondent noted that Putin has shown no sign of abandoning his main conditions for a settlement.

A limited pause in strikes – not a ceasefire

The US mission has coincided with a temporary halt in attacks on the two capitals.

The Kremlin said Putin had ordered Russian forces not to strike Kyiv for three days from midnight on Saturday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine, in turn, would refrain from attacks on Moscow through Monday. The arrangement is highly limited and does not amount to a nationwide ceasefire.

The next test will come in Kyiv, where Witkoff and Kushner are due to meet the Ukrainian leadership. Their visit will show whether the ideas discussed in Moscow can survive Ukraine’s own red lines — and whether the warmer tone from the Kremlin marks genuine diplomatic movement or simply another pause before negotiations stall again.

World.title: Netopia Payments expands license to include money remittance services after Romania’s Central Bank approval
World.content:
Romanian payments and technology platform Netopia Payments is entering a new stage of development after it received the authorization of the National Bank of Romania (BNR) to expand its payment institution license to include money remittance services, the company said.

The company, which processes more than RON 10 billion annually, is preparing new embedded finance solutions and developing an integrated financial platform for merchants, it said.

The company aims to expand its portfolio of services for merchants beyond traditional online payment processing and toward a comprehensive financial ecosystem.

At the same time, it is preparing to diversify the payment methods it accepts, including through the integration of account-to-account (A2A) solutions such as RoPay, and to expand financing options offered through partners, including merchant cash advance products.

Netopia’s priorities for the coming period include operationalizing its newly licensed activities, developing new financial products, and expanding its technology and operational infrastructure.

“Obtaining the license from the National Bank of Romania validates our security and compliance standards, but more importantly, it provides the foundation on which we are building Netopia’s future. Our vision is to become a comprehensive growth partner for entrepreneurs in Romania,” Raluca Micu, CEO of Netopia, said.

In the medium term, the company aims to build a one-stop shop model for merchants, a unified platform integrating multiple payment methods, rapid funds collection, automated transaction reconciliation, and complementary financial services.

Netopia Payments is a Romanian payments and technology platform for merchants, providing digital payment infrastructure and financial solutions to thousands of companies. Since 2023, private equity fund Innova Capital holds a majority stake in the company.

(Photo: the company)

World.title: Romanian construction company Concelex appoints Daniel Spiridon, Carol Șerban to strategy and transformation roles
World.content:
Romanian construction company Concelex announced it was strengthening its management team by bringing in two professionals with international backgrounds in strategy and transformation.

Daniel Spiridon, with over 20 years’ experience in management consulting and executive leadership, has joined Concelex as Deputy CEO Strategy.

World.title: Central Romania: Restored castle in Covasna reopens to the public
World.content:
The Miko Castle in the village of Olteni, Covasna County, which has been restored with EU funding, is set to reopen its doors on Saturday, September 5, Agerpresreported.

Built in 1827 by Count Miko Miklos, the castle is notable for the murals discovered on its interior walls during the restoration work. The paintings depict scenes from the social life of the period, as well as scenes from the Napoleonic Wars.

The property was returned to the descendants of Count Miko in 2007. Seven years later, they sold it to the Covasna County Council and the Bodoc Local Council.

The restoration was carried out as part of a project worth approximately RON 20 million, co-financed by EU funds through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR).

The castle will house the Székely Equestrian Museum, a section of the Székely National Museum in Sfântu Gheorghe.

The castle is also set to become part of the Transylvanian Manor Houses Route, one of 12 national cultural tourism routes financed through PNRR, the Covasna County Council said.

The reopening will also be marked by a screening of the Italian film Vita mia, directed by Edoardo Winspeare, which features several scenes filmed inside the castle. Other events for the opening weekend include a tour focusing on the history of the castle, and a guided tour of the Székely Equestrian Museum.

(Photo: Consiliul Județean Covasna)

World.title: Swedish man wanted over Stockholm shooting apprehended in Romania
World.content:
Romanian organized crime prosecutors have apprehended a Swedish citizen wanted by authorities in his home country over his alleged involvement in a shooting targeting two people in Stockholm. The suspect had lived in Romania for approximately three years, according to the Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT), as reported by Biziday.ro.

Prosecutors searched two properties in Bucharest and nearby Otopeni as part of an investigation into organized crime and aggravated murder.

According to investigators, several individuals tried to kill two people at a Stockholm address in September 2024. One of them allegedly fired at the building, with bullets passing through the entrance door and entering the home.

DIICOT said the suspect helped those involved in the attack, with his actions considered serious illegal threats aggravated by the use of a firearm.

Swedish authorities issued an arrest warrant for the man. He will be brought before a judge at the Bucharest Court of Appeal, with Romanian and Swedish law enforcement agencies cooperating in the case through Eurojust.

During the searches, authorities seized an air gun, a gas pistol, a bulletproof vest, quantities of plant material, data-storage devices, and bladed weapons.

According to DIICOT, another Swedish citizen suspected of belonging to a rival organized crime group was located in Romania in late July. A Romanian court ordered his detention pending extradition in connection with an alleged conspiracy to commit murder.

(Photo source: Inquam Photos/George Călin)

World.title: Estée Lauder Romania renews SkyTower lease, moves to new office
World.content:
Estée Lauder Romania has extended its lease at Bucharest’s SkyTower for a third time and relocated its headquarters to a newly fitted-out space on the building’s ninth floor. The beauty company has operated from the office tower since 2017.

The announcement did not disclose the duration or financial terms of the renewed lease, nor the size of the new office.

“This extension reflects our commitment to our team and our activities in Romania,” said Adrian Simionescu, country manager of Estée Lauder Romania.

The company also uses SkyTower’s SkyHub and board meeting areas to organize events.

Located in northern Bucharest, SkyTower is owned by Raiffeisen Property Holding International.

The 137-meter building has 37 floors and is Romania’s tallest office tower. Its underground structure extends to a depth of 60 meters and provides parking and storage space.

(Photo source: press release)

World.title: Romanian tech group Arobs sells Polish subsidiary to WB Electronics
World.content:
Arobs Transilvania Software, one of the largest technology companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange, has sold its entire stake in Arobs Polska to WB Electronics.

Before the sale, the company acquired the 5.66% stake held by Michal Drogosz, enabling the subsequent transfer to WB Electronics of 100% of the share capital of Arobs Polska, the company said in a filingwith the Bucharest Stock Exchange. The filing did not disclose the value of the transaction.

The decision to sell comes as the company pursues a focus on “areas where the group has established capabilities, can leverage international synergies and sees the most relevant growth opportunities.” These areas include software and engineering services for the automotive industry, IoT and telematics, enterprise software, life sciences and travel.

Arobs Polska focuses on developing electronic solutions for satellite applications, giving it a distinct profile compared with the group’s core business lines. Its activity is characterized by extended development cycles, projects carried out predominantly under institutional programs, and specific capital and infrastructure requirements, Arobs explained.

The integration of Arobs Polska into WB Electronics will ensure the continuity of ongoing projects and provide the team with access to an industrial platform and a portfolio of programs suited to the specific nature of its activities, the company said.

The transaction does not affect the current operations of Arobs Transilvania Software.

(Photo: Arobs Facebook Page)

World.title: Romanian court lifts house arrest for mercenary Horațiu Potra in alleged coup plot case
World.content:
Romania’s High Court of Cassation and Justice lifted the house arrest imposed on mercenary Horațiu Potra on Thursday, September 3, allowing him to remain free under judicial supervision while standing trial. The court granted Potra’s appeal against the previous preventive measure, Agerpres reported.

Horațiu Potra is one of the main defendants in a case concerning an alleged plot to destabilize Romania following the annulment of the 2024 presidential election.

The High Court released him from pre-trial detention in mid-June and placed him under house arrest, ordering him to wear an electronic monitoring bracelet. He had been in custody since November 2025, when he was brought back to Romania from Dubai together with his son and nephew.

Prosecutors indicted Potra on charges including attempted actions against the constitutional order, illegal possession of weapons and ammunition, violations of rules governing explosives and pyrotechnic materials, and public incitement. He is being tried alongside 20 alleged members of his mercenary group and former presidential candidate Călin Georgescu.

Prosecutors claim Horațiu Potra and his associates planned to infiltrate protests held after the December 2024 election annulment to provoke unrest and violent confrontations.

According to investigators, Cãlin Georgescu and his associates devised the plan during a meeting at a farm in Ciolpani shortly after the election was annulled. Potra allegedly coordinated efforts to bring a group of mercenaries to Bucharest and escalate the demonstrations into actions capable of destabilizing the constitutional order.

The allegations remain subject to examination by the court, and the defendants are presumed innocent until a final ruling.

(Photo source: Inquam Photos/Octav Ganea)

World.title: Romania’s 2026-2027 school year begins on September 7
World.content:
Students across Romania will return to classrooms on Monday, September 7, for the start of the 2026-2027 school year. The calendar includes 36 weeks of classes divided into five modules, with five holiday periods between them, Digi24 reported.

The school year officially runs administratively from September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027, but classes begin on September 7. Each school will determine the timetable for opening-day ceremonies, access for parents, and other activities.

World.title: Serbian, Bosnian Serb Officials Join Hundreds at Ratko Mladic Commemoration
World.content:
The man, who preferred to withhold his name, now lives in the Serbian capital. He decided to come along and pay tribute to Mladic, who he considers a “hero who defended his country” and who, in his view, Serbia “betrayed” when it extradited him to the UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague in 2011.

A large number of people with similar views, mostly men, gathered in front of the Army House before the commemoration began. Some of them were wearing T-shirts depicting Ratko Mladic, with messages expressing support for him.

Three men wearing identical T-shirts stood together and posed for journalists’ photos. As well as an image of Mladic, the shirts bear the phrases often used as a message of support for him: “General, are you afraid of anyone? ‘I fear no one but God.’”

World.title: Serbia’s Vucic Slates EU Condemnation of Mladic Tributes as ‘Stupid’
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos cancelled her planned visit to EU candidate state Serbia on Friday, the day after Ratko Mladic’s body was transported on a government plane to Belgrade, where it was met by officials and an army honour guard.

Groups of supporters of the former Bosnian Serb military chief also greeted the motorcade carrying his body into Belgrade with banners praising Mladic, hung from roadway overpasses, with messages such as “Thank you, General” and “Welcome home, General”.

“The return of his remains to Belgrade reminds Europe of the darkest pages in our recent history,” Kos wrote on X.

“The glorification surrounding his death is incompatible with the values on which the EU path is built … The values that underpin our common future are not negotiable. In this context, I have decided not to proceed with my planned visit to Serbia at this time,” she added.

Her criticisms have been echoed by ministers from several other EU member states.

Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic dismissed Kos’s criticism as “extremely brief, but stupid, as usual”.

“‘Glorification’ of General Ratko Mladic, except it doesn’t say who was glorifying anything. And when they can’t find anything concrete, then they deal with underpasses and overpasses [where pro-Mladic banners were displayed]. I suppose we were meant to ban people from showing up, to ban the funeral,” he told the media on Friday.

Mladic’s body was returned to Serbia on Thursday evening on a Serbian government plane.

Ratko Mladic’s son, Darko, confirmed on Friday that the funeral will be held on Monday at the Topcider Cemetery in Belgrade.

Before the funeral, a tribute to Mladic will be held in a church where the coffin will be placed, and on Saturday, a public commemoration will be staged at the Home of the Army of Serbia, in central Belgrade.

Darko Mladic said a procession would be organised on Monday from the church to the cemetery and emphasised that he expects a large turnout.

“This is a people’s funeral, and, as you all know, I do not engage in politics and would not mix politics into this. The only thing I can say is that regarding our requests [to the Hague for Mladic’s conditional release because of illness], of which there were many in the past, President [Vucic] was always there for us, and I would like to publicly thank him for that support in defending General Mladic, which meant a lot to us,” Darko Mladic said.

Neither Darko Mladic nor the Minister of Justice, Nenad Vujic, who was sitting next to him at the press conference, specified whether there would be army or state honours at the funeral.

On August 27, when Mladic died, Vujic initially said Mladic would be buried with state honours. “General Mladic is a general and there are protocols that apply,” he said then.

Mladic held the rank of general in the Yugoslav People’s Army, JNA, during the 1990s but legal experts in Serbia are divided on whether there is any basis for a funeral with state or army honours, given that he was convicted of genocide.

President Vucic has since cast doubt on the idea of a funeral with state honours. Minister Vujic on Friday, when quizzed about state honours, just said that the state would provide all the family was entitled to, out of “respect for the family’s wishes … [and] according to the laws of the state of Serbia”.

Asked whether he will attend the funeral in person, Vucic on Friday pleaded a packed schedule. “I have an official visit from the President of Uzbekistan [Shavkat Mirziyoyev] for the whole day on Monday and Tuesday, scheduled four months ago,” he said.

Several European dignitaries have echoed EU commissioner Kos in criticising the glorification of Mladic.

Belgium’s Foreign Minister, Maxime Prevot, wrote on X on Friday that “it is shameful and disrespectful to the victims and their families to reserve such honours for his funeral.

“It’s a step distancing Serbia from EU’s fundamental values of respect for human dignity, human rights and the fight against impunity – going in the opposite direction of what is expected from a EU candidate country,” Prevot said.

Ireland’s Minister for European Affairs and Defence, Thomas Byrne, told media on Friday that it was “not acceptable” if there were “senior figures from government memorialising that man”.

World.title: Kosovo Charges Serbian Security Officers Over Jashari Compound Massacre
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Blerim Isufaj (C), Chief Prosecutor at the Kosovo Special Prosecution, with prosecutor Valdet Gashi on September 4, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

Kosovo’s Special Prosecution announced on Friday that it has filed an indictment charging 35 suspects with involvement in the murder of 26 civilians at the compound of Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA commander Adem Jashari in the village of Prekaz in Skenderaj/Srbica in March 1998.

“After years of work, we have succeeded in finalising the investigation into the Prekaz case by filing an indictment. We have managed to substantiate the well-founded suspicion that the accused committed the criminal offence of war crimes against the civilian population – specifically on March 5, 6, and 7, 1998, in the village of Prekaz, more precisely in the Jashari neighbourhood,” prosecutor Valdet Gashi said.

BIRN has seen the indictment which, among others, includes the names of Jovica Stanisic, the former head of the Serbian State Security Service; Vlastimir Djordjevic, a former high-ranking Serbian Interior Ministry official; Sreten Lukic, a wartime head of the Serbian interior ministry’s staff for Kosovo and Milorad ‘Legija’ Ulemek, a former commander of Serbia’s State Security Unit for Special Operations.

“Based on material and testimonial evidence, we have identified 35 accused individuals in this case who held high command positions within the Serbian special police units,” Gashi added.

Serbian police and military forces besieged the Jashari family compound in Prekaz from March 5 to 7, 1998, leaving 59 dead, including the founder of the KLA, Adem Jashari, himself.

The assault caused outrage among Kosovo Albanians and is seen as the incident that encouraged widespread armed resistance against Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic’s regime.

Gashi told media on Friday that the indictment was filed in absentia as the authorities could not secure the presence of the suspects.

Stanisic is currently serving a sentence for war crimes in another case after being convicted by the Hague Tribunal, while Ulemek is in prison for his role in the killing of Serbian Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic. Djordjevic and Lukic have been released after serving war crimes sentences for other crimes.

Chief Special Prosecution Prosecutor Blerim Isufaj highlighted the indictment as “the first one concerning the killing of civilians in the Jashari family compound in Prekaz, Skenderaj”.

In cases concerning war crimes committed during the 1998-99 Kosovo war, legal cooperation between Kosovo and Serbia remains almost non-existent, so it appears unlikely that most of the indictees will be available for trial.

World.title: Serbian President Launches ‘Non-Political’ Podcast as Election Looms
World.content:
Ahead of elections expected in the next few months, Serbia’s head of state has started doing podcasts, while promising to give politics a big miss on his show.

The first episode of Vucic’s PodcAVst aired on Friday at noon on his official YouTube channel. In it, Vucic interviewed the basketball coach Miroslav “Muta” Nikolic, introducing him as a “pal” and a “legend of Serbian basketball”.

“When I was a boy, I applied to become a radio reporter. At the time, my dream was to become a sports commentator or reporter. I didn’t make it – Radio Belgrade rightly rejected me because I had a slight speech impediment,” Vucic reminisced in the introduction.

Vucic said he decided to try the podcast format for a simple reason: to have conversations with successful people.

“I’ve missed having conversations with successful people, with people who are different from me, so that I can learn something from them, gain a different perspective and listen to them, rather than having them listen to me,” he said.

“I’ll try not to be someone who argues or disagrees with guests, but instead to be here to learn as much as possible from people working in completely different fields. And there won’t be a single word about politics,” he added.

During the interview, Vucic and Nikolic spoke about basketball strategies, teams, players and coaches. They also reminisced about Vucic’s own sports efforts and his brother Andrej’s life.

Since the podcast premiered live, it had a live chat filled with supportive comments like “Serbia Wins” and “Serbia United”, and emojis including the Serbian flag, a wolf, hearts and flexed biceps. Some presented opposing views, however, such as “The students will win against Vucic”, referencing the wave of student-led protests against his government.

By launching his own podcast, Vucic is following a trend already embraced by political figures in the region, notably Albania’s Edi Rama with his weekly “Flasim” (“Let’s Talk”) podcast, as well as politicians further afield, such as California Governor Gavin Newsom and US Senator Ted Cruz. It has not been announced when Vucic’s next show will be aired.

The podcast’s launch comes amid Vucic’s already extensive presence in traditional media ahead of nationwide elections expected to be held in the coming months.

According to Serbian election watchdog CRTA, by August 18 he had made 64 live television appearances that month, already surpassing his previous monthly record of 61, set in March 2025.

World.title: Week in Review: Ghosts and Guns
World.content:
Bosnian Serb military chief Ratko Mladic died in The Hague at the age of 84 on August 27, having spent his final years serving a life sentence for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes. BIRN covered the death of Mladic extensively, with profiles, features, analyses and opinion articles.

Mladic’s death has shown just how far the former Bosnian Serb military chief’s legacy extends beyond the judgments that established his responsibility for some of the worst atrocities of the Bosnian war.

Across Bosnia’s mainly Serb Republika Srpska entity, Mladic supporters took to the streets, lit candles and publicly celebrated Mladic, including in towns where his forces committed crimes, while politicians in both Bosnia and Serbia joined in paying tribute. For genocide survivors, the sight of young people who may not even have been born during the war glorifying Mladic was particularly disturbing, proving that nationalist narratives have passed to another generation.

The reactions have also prompted deeper questions about what justice has achieved. Former Hague Tribunal intern Ahmet Gumusbas observed that Mladic’s conviction established criminal responsibility and an authoritative record of the crimes, but could never end disputes over memory and denial. Journalist Kristina Ljevak Bajramovic reflected on the gulf between Mladic, who was able to grow old, and the thousands of his victims who were denied that chance.

In Serbia, meanwhile, Youth Initiative for Human Rights director Sofija Todorovic argued that official tributes to Mladic demonstrate how the glorification of convicted war criminals has become embedded in Serbia’s politics, media and public life.

World.title: Romania Opens New Human Trafficking Case Against Tate Brothers
World.content:
Andrew and Tristan Tate arrive at court for a pre-trial hearing in Bucharest, February 2024. Photo: EPA-EFE/Robert Ghement.

Romanian anti-organised crime prosecutors on Thursday evening indicted British-American influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate in a new case involving alleged trafficking of minors, according to court records seen by BIRN.

Prosecutors accuse the defendants, together with two Romanian nationals, of trafficking minors and related offences, including money laundering.

The new indictment follows a December 2024 decision by the Bucharest Court of Appeal to return the original case file to prosecutors for the investigation to be redone.

Romania’s anti-organised crime agency, DIICOT, subsequently expanded its investigation and brought additional charges.

According to judicial sources cited by online publication HotNews, some of the allegations have been separated from the broader investigation in order to avoid the risk of statutory limitation.

The brothers have been under investigation in Romania since their initial arrest in December 2022.

They face various allegations, including human trafficking, rape, trafficking of minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money-laundering.

In June, prosecutors expanded their investigation into Andrew Tate to cover new allegations that he sexually exploited a woman in 2017, taking advantage of her vulnerable situation to induce her to produce sexually explicit content and perform video chat activities – and that he and his brother, Tristan, laundered almost 3 million euros earned from human trafficking via two companies between 2018 and 2022.

The Tate brothers have denied wrongdoing.

Despite being arrested in 2022, the case against them has made slow progress: in late 2024, a court returned the original indictment to prosecutors, saying it was flawed, and in February 2025 DIICOT permitted the brothers to leave Romania, despite the ongoing case.

They are currently in the United States, contesting extradition to the United Kingdom, where authorities have brought nearly 60 charges against them, including rape, human trafficking and sexual exploitation.

Both brothers have described the cases against them as politically motivated and unfounded.

World.title: Democracy Digest: Poland Investigates Arson of Drone Factory as Suspected Russian Sabotage
World.content:
Hungary PM looks to recover ECJ fines; Orban’s son central figure in Chad mission

Statements made by PM Peter Magyar this week indicate that Hungary might not be the kind of pliant partner the EU had hoped for after his predecessor, Viktor Orban, was turfed out of office. Magyar met with Manfred Weber, leader of the European People’s Party (EPP), and European Council President Antonio Costa earlier this week, and made clear he would strongly defend Hungary’s rights and interests during the talks over the next seven-year EU budget (MFF). Magyar said in a Facebook post that his Tisza party would like to become a full member of the EPP, the European political family of centre-right parties that Orban’s Fidesz left in 2021 before being expelled. However, before that can happen, the Article 7 procedure – a punitive measure which removes voting rights of member states – against Hungary would have to be closed, he said. The procedure was launched by the European Parliament in 2018, but needs a formal decision by the Council of the EU to end the process. Magyar also touched on the sensitive subject of the 1 million euros that Hungary is paying daily for failing to comply with EU asylum regulations. The case dates back to the Orban government’s decision to close the controversial transit zones at the border, while making it next-to-impossible to submit asylum applications from inside Hungary. Under the current system, asylum applications can only be submitted at Hungarian embassies in Belgrade or Kyiv. Last year, Hungary received 113 asylum applications and granted refugee status, subsidiary or humanitarian protection to just 35 people. Weber reportedly offered to help in settling the issue, but Magyar stressed the border fence will have to remain in place. Reopening the transit zones would be highly controversial, as the opposition would use it as evidence Magyar is bowing to pressure from Brussels. On the other hand, the fines have already reached around 1 billion euros – a significant loss of revenue for the Hungarian budget. Magyar floated the idea of recovering this money in the framework of the MFF negotiations. In another move likely to be frowned on in Brussels, the Hungarian government blocked Ukraine’s EU accession process for the third time this week, arguing insufficient progress on minority rights.

The family of former PM Orban was back in the headlines this week as documents obtained by news site 444.hu confirmed what had long been suspected – that Orban’s son, Gaspar, was the driving force behind Hungary’s planned military mission to Chad (and not the wild conspiracy theory of Hungary serving Russian interests in the region). The idea originated during a trip to Niger in May 2023 by Orban Jnr and Tristan Azbej, Hungary’s deputy state secretary responsible for helping persecuted Christians. The two initially planned an agricultural project there – a model camel farm supported by the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences. Farmers from Niger would have been instructed by Hungarian experts on how to process camel milk and produce dairy products. However, after a military coup in Niger in 2023 attention shifted to Chad, where the project’s aims were significantly expanded. In addition to the planned model farm, it was to include a medical and a military mission involving up to 200 Hungarian soldiers. According to the documents now obtained, Orban Jnr functioned as the pro-forma leader and central coordinator of the project. Virtually all major decisions – from when to buy plane tickets for experts to arranging the shipment of medical equipment – depended on him. In a previous interview, former defence minister Kristof Szalay-Bobrovniczky had tried to defend the mission and Orban Jnr’s role in it: “Gaspar Orban is a military officer… He goes wherever he is ordered to go. I assigned him as a liaison officer.” The newly published documents prove otherwise. In the end, the Chad government lost enthusiasm for the project. Although 27 billion forints (73.5 million euros) were earmarked for the mission in the 2026 budget, the plan was quietly shelved by Orban as the April election approached.

World.title: Significant Weather Change Coming to Croatia
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – A drastic weather change is on the cards for Croatia, bringing relief from oppressive, scorching temperatures.

Index reports that Croatia is currently under the influence of an anticyclone that is bringing clear, stable and hot weather with an inflow of dry air from northern Africa. It won’t last long, however, as a major change is approaching next week. While three tropical cyclones are currently moving across the Pacific, driven by El Niño, and the Atlantic hurricane season is lagging, a deep cyclone between Iceland and Great Britain is slowly shifting eastwards and will affect the weather in continental Europe.

the genoa cyclone

A ridge of high pressure over Scandinavia, connected to the anticyclone over central Europe, extends all the way to northern Africa and the Black Sea. However, a cyclone from the Atlantic will descend towards the North Sea, and its surge of cold and unstable air over western and central Europe will be blocked by the Alps. The jet stream that will bypass the Alps on the western side will trigger the rapid development of a new cyclone in the Gulf of Genoa. That Genoa cyclone, together with the jet stream and a cold front, will begin to influence the weather in Croatia from the middle of next week.

showers, thunderstorms and a significant pressure drop is looming

Before the front actually arrives, due to southerly and south-westerly flow, a strong jugo (sirocco) will blow. The inflow of moisture will further intensify the feeling of sultriness. According to current forecast models, the cold front will affect the northwestern inland areas as well as the northern and central Adriatic during the night from Wednesday to Thursday. During Thursday it will spread across the whole country. The front will be accompanied by thunderstorms, showers and rain, along with strong, locally stormy winds. After the front passes, a strong, locally stormy bora will start blowing in the northern Adriatic. Air temperatures inland will drop by 12 to 15 degrees, and on the Adriatic and in the coastal areas by 8 to 10 degrees.

there’s still a few more days of heat to go

Before the major weather change, we can still expect a few more days of heat. Moderate heatwave warnings from the DHMZ (Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service) have been issued for today, tomorrow and Tuesday. Today it will be sunny and hot with a weak north-westerly wind, while on the Adriatic the maestral will blow. Towards the end of the day and during the night there may be a weak bura in the Velebit coastal area. The DHMZ has issued a heatwave warning for the Adriatic that will last until the middle of the week. Sea temperatures are between 25 and 28 degrees.

On Monday and Tuesday predominantly sunny, warm and hot weather continues. Morning temperatures inland will be around 17°C and on the Adriatic around 23°C. Maximum daytime temperatures inland will range from 30 to 31°C, while on the Adriatic they will reach around 34°C, with a weak to moderate maestral.

On Wednesday the jugo will start blowing, and daytime temperatures will still be high, hovering around 32°C inland and up to 35°C on the Adriatic and islands. In the evening and during the night a gradual increase in cloud cover is expected from the northwest, along with the arrival of the cold front.

World.title: Goodbye Toll Booths: Croatia introducing Crolibertas
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – Croatia is set to introduce Crolibertas early next year as the country finally bids farewell to toll booths.

Poslovni reports that as of the beginning of March 2027, Croatia will abandon the system of toll booths and introduce a fully electronic toll collection system called Crolibertas. Croatia is preparing for a “traffic revolution” that should permanently erase the images of kilometre-long queues in front of toll booths during the summer months. With planned implementation starting on the 1st of March 2027, a new, fully electronic toll collection system named Crolibertas is coming into force. This will consign to history the model of stopping, taking a ticket and paying on exit from the motorway, replacing it with a free-flow traffic system.

It is important to emphasise straight away that, despite the digitalisation, Croatia is not introducing vignettes along the lines of Slovenia or Austria. Tolls will continue to be charged according to the distance travelled and the vehicle category, meaning drivers will pay only for the distance they actually travel on the motorway. The main change lies in the technology and method of collection, which will be automated, faster and more efficient, with the aim of reducing congestion, shortening travel times and cutting harmful emissions caused by stop-start driving.

how it will work

The new system will operate on the basis of so-called “Multi-Lane Free Flow” (MLFF) technology. Instead of the existing toll plazas, portals equipped with cameras and sensors will be installed along the entire motorway network. The system will rely on a combination of two proven technologies: Automatic Licence Plate Recognition (ALPR), which will be the primary solution for light vehicles such as passenger cars and motorcycles and DSRC technology, i.e. communication via the existing ENC devices.

Drivers of light vehicles will have a choice: they can register in the system and link their licence plate to a valid payment method (such as a bank card), or they can continue using an ENC device as before. However, for heavy goods vehicles weighing more than 3.5 tonnes, the use of an ENC device will be mandatory. This ensures that all traffic, regardless of vehicle type, can pass without stopping.

what tourists and foreign drivers need to do

For tourists and foreign nationals, who make up a significant portion of summer traffic, advance preparation will be key. In order to use the motorways smoothly, they will need to register their vehicle in the Crolibertas system in advance. This can be done in several ways: via the central internet portal or mobile app (the most recommended option, so everything can be sorted out before setting off). For those who do not do this in advance, rapid registration will be available on special lanes at motorway entrances (at the locations of the current toll plazas), as well as at physical sales points such as HAC offices or petrol stations.

To avoid any delays, drivers are strongly advised to complete registration online. Special attention should be paid to the accuracy of the entered licence plate data and the validity of the linked payment method, as even the smallest error can lead to charging problems and potential fines.

existing enc users

Existing ENC device users will not need to buy new ones. They will be able to continue using their devices, but with one key change: it will be mandatory to link the existing ENC device to the vehicle’s licence plate.

associated costs and coverage

Regarding prices, Croatian Motorways (HAC) say that the introduction of the new system itself should not lead to an increase in tolls. A new tariff study is being prepared that could introduce more flexible charging models, for example lower prices for travel outside peak periods, which would further relieve traffic. The single electronic toll collection system will cover the entire motorway network in Croatia, including the sections managed by the concessionaires Bina-Istra and Autocesta Zagreb-Macelj. This means drivers will need only one single system for the whole country.

World.title: Croatian Government: New Package of Measures Coming Soon
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – The Croatian Government is currently preparing to present a new autumn package of measures, with nuclear energy part of the discussion.

Croatia has taken a new step towards the possible construction of a nuclear power plant. Ana Blaskovic reports for Poslovni that on Friday, the Croatian Government tasked the Ministry of Economy with launching a structured information procedure and talks with potential suppliers of nuclear technologies and partner countries. Concrete and comparable information will be requested from them on available technologies, technical characteristics and economic conditions.

The process is currently non-binding and does not represent a decision to build a power plant, the government emphasises. However, among the technologies that will be considered are small modular and advanced modular reactors. After the talks, the Ministry will consolidate the collected data and submit a report to the Government. Prime Minister Andrej Plenković announced that at the next session, the government will present the autumn package of measures to mitigate the consequences of the energy crisis for the general public and the economy. The package comes after inflation accelerated to 4.1 percent in August, primarily due to the rise in energy prices, which increased by 17.4 percent on an annual basis.

The government currently expects the upcoming autumn measures to mitigate the impact of energy price increases caused by the crisis still going on over in the Middle East. In addition, through amendments to the Crafts Act, those with crafts will be somewhat financially relieved as chamber contributions will be reduced from two to 1.5 percent of the basic personal allowance, and a novelty is the introduction of status innovations such as the institute of family crafts.

World.title: Croatian Population Rose by a Mere 8,760 in 2025
World.content:
September the 6th, 2026 – The Croatian population rose by just 8,760 in 2025, which is representative of a 0.2% increase.

According to the mid-2025 population estimate, Croatia had just 3,874,993 inhabitants (1,893,472 men and 1,981,521 women). Poslovni reports that compared with the previous year’s estimate, the population increased by 8,760 people, or 0.2%. The continuous and deeply concerning ageing of the population continued in 2025.

Istria County recorded the largest relative increase: +1.60%, while growth was also recorded in: Zadar, Zagreb County, Dubrovnik-Neretva, Lika-Senj, Split-Dalmatia, Šibenik-Knin and Primorje-Gorski Kotar counties. The City of Zagreb specifically grew by 0.45%. The remaining counties saw population declines. The sharpest relative drops were in Sisak-Moslavina (−1.14%) and Požega-Slavonia (−1.13%).

a constantly ageing population

The average age of the total population was 44.7 years (men 42.9, women 46.4), placing Croatia among the oldest nations in Europe. The highest share of people aged 65+ relative to the total population was recorded in Šibenik-Knin County (28.8%). The lowest share of all was seen in the City of Zagreb (20.9%). The share of young people (0–19 years) in the total population was just 18.7%. The lowest share of young people was recorded in Primorje-Gorski Kotar (16.2%), while the highest was recorded in Međimurje County (21.1%).

The share of the fertile contingent (women aged 15–49) in the total female population was also a very worrying 39.8%.

over half of the country lives in just 5 counties

52.5% of Croatia’s population lives in just five counties. The City of Zagreb is home to 20.1% (777,744 people), Split-Dalmatia County is home to 11.1% (431,463 people). The least populated were Lika-Senj County: 43,402 (1.1%) and Požega-Slavonia County: 60,289 (1.6%).

natural change and migration

In 2025, 32,479 births were registered across Croatia (410 more than in 2024), while 50,007 deaths were recorded (1,073 fewer than in 2024). The natural increase remained negative at −17,528 (slightly better than the previous year). Marriages and divorces also both rose. There were 17,270 marriages (+64 compared with 2024) and 5,674 divorces. (+713 compared with 2024).

As far as net migration is concerned, it stood at +19,180 (almost half the 2024 figure of +31,394).

World.title: HNS Confirms: Luka Modrić Continues With National Team
World.content:
Croatia national team captain Luka Modrić will be on the squad list that head coach Slaven Bilić announces on Monday for the Nations League fixtures against Czechia, Spain and England.

Modrić has confirmed to Bilić and Croatian Football Federation (HNS) president Marijan Kustić that he remains available for the national team in the new edition of the Nations League. The legendary international career of a player who has left an indelible mark across 202 caps for Croatia and led the country to its greatest successes will thus continue.

“Of course I’m delighted by Luka’s decision, because we all know what he represents and means for Croatia, both on and off the pitch. I’m especially pleased that after 14 years we’ll be working together again, sharing the strong ambition for Croatia to be strong, successful and on a par with the best in the world,” said head coach Slaven Bilić.

The head coach will unveil the squad list on Monday ahead of the September gathering for matches against Czechia (26 September, in Prague), Spain (29 September, in Seville), England (3 October, in Rijeka) and Spain again (6 October, in Split).

World.title: Dubrovnik Getting New Transatlantic Route: From May 2027 Direct to Montreal
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – Dubrovnik is set to get a new transatlantic route from May 2027, linking the Pearl of the Adriatic with Montreal directly.

Dubrovnik will be directly connected to Montreal from May 2027. Canada’s largest airline, Air Canada, is introducing a seasonal route between the two cities, with the first flight announced for 11 May 2027. As reported by DuList, the new route is part of Air Canada’s expansion for the 2027 summer season, during which the company is also introducing several other new international destinations, including Oslo, Basel, Shannon and Guangzhou.

For Dubrovnik specifically, this is an important step in strengthening direct connectivity with the North American market. Montreal is one of Air Canada’s more significant hubs, so the new route will also open up onward travel options for passengers from Dubrovnik to other Canadian and American cities.

According to data from Air Canada’s sales system, tickets for the new route have already appeared on sale. A return economy-class ticket for travel from 12 to 26 June 2027 is currently selling, for example, for around 1,256 Canadian dollars. Prices can of course change depending on the travel dates and availability. Air Canada has previously operated services to Croatia, and this time the choice has fallen on Dubrovnik. The new route could additionally contribute to attracting Canadian visitors and to extending the tourist season, given that operations begin as early as mid-May. A detailed flight schedule, including the exact number of weekly rotations and the end of seasonal operations, has not yet been published.

World.title: Secrets of Cape Škamica – Forgotten Sundial From Southern Pag Saved
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – Cape Škamica is a very isolated point, and a long-forgotten sundial from this southern part of the island of Pag has been saved.

On the solitary Cape Škamica on the southern part of the island of Pag, an unusual stone monument – a historic sundial – has been saved from decay. Ana Zunic reports for Morski that following years of exposure to the harsh bura wind, salt and the blows of the jugo, the object that bears witness to past times has been successfully reconstructed. Despite the restoration, it still keeps its greatest secret to itself, and that is that no one knows with certainty who built it and exactly when.

Archaeological research in Zadar and Split has so far offered no concrete written traces or plans. Local tradition attributes the construction to Jure Komadina from Vlašići, citing the similarity of the building technique with a nearby village well, while another theory places the origin of the structure in the era of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy.

fishermen and shepherds knew it well

Although historical documents are lacking, testimonies of older locals confirm that the sundial truly served its purpose. Roman numerals were once carved into it and an iron pin was fitted that cast a shadow to indicate the time. Located on an important maritime corridor – with a view of the Pag Bridge, Velebit and the islets of Mali and Veliki Sikavac, the sundial served for centuries as a key landmark for shepherds from Vlašići and Smokvica and fishermen from Vrsi. Before the recent intervention the structure was in extremely poor condition, without binding material and with significantly damaged plaster. The comprehensive restoration was financially supported by the City of Pag and the Municipality of Vrsi, with the involvement of the association “Volim Vlašići”, experts Šime Stojak and Šime Glavan, and the contractor Travej d.o.o. The archaeological survey and documentation were prepared by archaeologists Neda and Igor Kulenović, under the conservator supervision of Ivan Matković.

both roman and arabic numerals are on the sundial

During the reconstruction the damaged stone blocks were replaced, and both Roman numerals (for winter time reckoning) and Arabic numerals (for summer time reckoning) were precisely carved into the new plaster, along with half-hour markings. The entire construction was finally protected with a special impregnation. The initiative launched back in 2020 has thus finally reached its conclusion, but the work is not finished. Although the monument has been saved, it still does not have formal status as a cultural asset, which is why the initiators will submit a proposal to the City of Pag for its protection and entry into the Register of Cultural Assets of the Republic of Croatia.

The site has already become part of the Pag Outdoor tourist offer; an approximately four-kilometre-long hiking trail leads to it from the direction of Vlašići and Smokvica. Plans also include the installation of an information board that will acquaint visitors with the history, restoration and the mystery that still surrounds this stone monument on Cape Škamica.

World.title: Men Removed From Croatia After Glorifying Ratko Mladić in Dubrovnik
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – Several men, some of whom are citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, have been removed from Croatia after glorifying war criminal Ratko Mladić in the Dubrovnik area.

Police officers working for the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration have now conducted criminal investigations that ran from the 28th of August to the 2nd of September 2026. Morski reports that those investigations were launched against four citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were temporarily in Croatia (aged 31, 30, 25 and 25) and against one 35-year-old Croatian citizen.

All of the men were arrested for publishing content which glorified and supported Ratko Mladić. The police conducted the criminal investigations after receiving several reports from members of the public. It was established that the men, on publicly accessible social media profiles, had published pictures, symbols, songs and texts with which they paid tribute to and expressed gratitude to Mladić.

expulsion from croatia for the non-citizens

Three of the men who are citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina have already been brought before the Municipal Court in Dubrovnik, where they were non-finally found guilty and issued with monetary fines. After that, their residence and work permits will be revoked and their short-term stay in Croatia terminated, with a three-month ban on entry into the country.

Proceedings for expulsion from the European Economic Area with a two-year entry ban have also been initiated against them; the ban will take effect after the judgement becomes final. The fourth foreign national, as well as the Croatian citizen, will also be brought before the Municipal Court in Dubrovnik.

World.title: Pärnu flood situation stable but work continues
World.content:
Heavy rain hit Pärnu on Friday morning, overwhelming the sewer system, but the city government said the situation is now under control.

Streets and roads were flooded and water entered buildings. Rainfall exceeded 100 millimeters, reaching more than 120 millimeters in some places. Employees of Pärnu City Government, water utility Pärnu Vesi, the Rescue Board and the Estonian Rescue Association are continuously monitoring and assessing the situation.

"The heavy rainfall also affected our neighboring municipality. Yesterday evening, we gathered at the Rescue Board's command center, after which the mayor of Tori Municipality and I inspected the most critical areas in Pärnu and Tori Municipality. At the height of the crisis, both local governments had to focus all their attention on helping their own residents, but once the situation stabilized, we were able to assess the situation in the neighboring municipality as well and share our experiences," Deputy Mayor Sander Kilk said.

Water levels in Pärnu are falling, although water continues to flow in from Rääma bog. The Rescue Board's pumps and the city's systems are currently able to cope with the situation. The Rescue Board will decide when pumping can be stopped.

The city government is also asking residents to check on their neighbors, acquaintances and elderly people. Anyone who needs assistance is asked to report it. The Pärnu City Government information line at 444 8200 is answering calls around the clock.

Temporary traffic changes remain in effect. Road users are asked to remain alert, follow traffic signs and, where possible, avoid areas where the effects of flooding are still disrupting traffic. Traffic arrangements may change and roads will be reopened as soon as possible.

Kilk said good cooperation between different agencies, local governments and volunteers has been crucial during the crisis.

"We are extremely grateful to our various partners. Several rescue crews from across Estonia have traveled to Pärnu to help, while experts have also provided us with the latest data and expertise, which have been extremely useful in making decisions. I want to sincerely thank all the rescuers, volunteers and others who have come to help from across Estonia. It is thanks to you that the situation is under control today and people have received the assistance they need," Kilk said.

Important contacts:

If someone's health or life is in danger, call 112.

Pärnu Vesi: 445 5660

Pärnu City Government information line: 444 8200
